#### A44 amendment — round 2 findings from the Developer report on #540 (Architect, 2026-10-20)

All three are class design; none changes a `hooks/git-guardrails` Interface or adds a Seam.

1. **`preflight-not-reachable-in-adopted-projects`: decided, no scaffolding; call it through `.guardrails/source/`.**
   - *Fact.* `lib/codex-adoption.py` (install, line ~129) unconditionally sets the link `.guardrails/source` to the source checkout on every `adopt.sh --runtime codex` run, and validates its ownership on re-run and status (line ~70). So for every Codex adoption the path the Codex text names is populated by the same step that provides `session-context.sh`, which that text already requires from the same path. `merge-preflight.sh` resolves its own directory with `pwd -P`, so the symlink resolves to the real checkout and `hooks/git-guardrails` is found; the guard runs against the caller's cwd (the project checkout). No new reachability problem exists beyond the one the Codex mapping already carries.
   - *Rejected.* Scaffolding a copy like `wait-for-ci.sh`: a copy drifts from the guard it must match, and would need a template plus a sync check for a script that is only a shallow wrapper (it earns its place by being a thin path to the deep guard, not by being local). Deferring into the 5b hook-install follow-up: not needed, the path works today. Claude-adopted projects do not get the script and do not need it (the hook runs).
   - *In scope for #540 (S):* test only, no production change. Add one scenario: run the preflight through a symlinked directory (as `.guardrails/source` is) from a different cwd, with the project as cwd and a behind PR; expect the guard's block (exit 2, reason on stderr), proving the `pwd -P` resolution and cwd handling that adopted projects depend on. Wording in `adapters/codex/INSTRUCTIONS.md` stays.
2. **`preflight-escape-hatch-env`: confirmed as built, with the semantics stated; not a widening.**
   - *Fact.* The guard reads `CLAUDE_WORKFLOW_MERGE_GUARD_OFF` only from the command text, by design (comment at the loop in `hooks/git-guardrails`: a command that has not started cannot influence the guard's environment; the visible prefix is what makes the hatch deliberate and auditable). The preflight is itself the command being started, so an env var on its invocation (`CLAUDE_WORKFLOW_MERGE_GUARD_OFF=1 ./merge-preflight.sh 5`) is the same per-invocation, visible-in-the-command-text act; the script just forwards it into the synthesized text so the guard prints its loud skip warning. Only an exported, ambient variable is wider than the Claude form, and it buys nothing: the preflight is voluntary (a session can simply not run it, no hatch needed), and the skip is still reported loudly.
   - *Decision.* Keep as built. Developer: no code change; the header comment should say the intended use is as an invocation prefix (one comment line). No new scenario beyond S342(d).
3. **No-target case with two open PRs for the current branch fails open: accepted.** It is the same rule as A44 1(b) applied to both branch-shaped inputs, matches Open decision 5a (ambiguity fails open) and the resolver's own header ("no first-match-wins guess between candidates"); the previous first-match behaviour was the inconsistency. Two open PRs sharing a head name means fork PRs, where guessing could check the wrong PR. Work: one scenario so the change is deliberate (no target, two matching PRs, exit 0 with the existing warning); S337's S339/S340 cover the named-branch twins only.
- **Work list.** QA (S): the two scenarios above (symlinked-path preflight, no-target ambiguity). Developer (S): implement them red-first per QA, plus the one comment line. Nothing for `ORCHESTRATOR.md`, stamp, or `CHANGES.md`.
- **Update after Human decision 4 on #516 (5b answered yes, hook install filed as #544).** Item 1 stands and stays in #540: #540 ships only the voluntary `merge-preflight.sh`, which is reachable today through `.guardrails/source/`; its one test is cheap and verifies what the shipped Codex text claims. #544 (hook install) does not need the preflight's reachability and does not change this decision; it makes the preflight a fallback for sessions without trusted hooks. No scaffolding goes into #544 on this account.

### A45 — SessionStart creates missing skill links through one create-only module; `adopt.sh` stays the owner of refresh and cleanup (#505; F6, F9, S9)

- **Why:** `pending-changes.sh` only warns that a skill has no link in `.claude/skills/`; this repo ignored that line for 12 days. Human decisions 1-3 on #505 (2026-10-20): a dangling link is left alone, a missing `.claude/skills/` is created, and a non-gitignored `.claude/skills/` means create nothing and warn. A45 is the next free A (A44 highest on `main`; no remote branch claims A45).
- **Module and placement.** New `lib/skill-links.sh` (sourced, bash 3.2, same pattern as `lib/changes.sh` and `lib/nfr.sh`) with one function. `pending-changes.sh` calls it and keeps printing the existing warning for whatever the module reports as not created. Decided on Depth and Locality: the logic (adoption test, ignore test, per-path rules, fail-open) is about 40 lines behind a two-argument Interface, and it is the only code in the hook path that mutates the project, so it gets its own file and its own header comment, which keeps `pending-changes.sh`'s "no mutation" statement true everywhere else and makes the exception visible. Rejected: inline in `pending-changes.sh` (buries the one mutation in a 400-line report script); extraction from `adopt.sh` (see next point).
- **No extraction from `adopt.sh`.** `skill_symlink_update` replaces symlinks, the hook must not; the only shared fact is the link form `<workflow_dir>/skills/<name>`, one `ln -s`. Two policies behind one function would need a mode flag, a shallow, wider Interface. Deletion test on a shared helper: complexity does not reappear in callers, so it would be a pass-through. Drift in the link form is caught by a test instead: a link made by the hook must equal (same `readlink`) the one `adopt.sh` makes for the same skill. `adopt.sh` is not edited.
- **Interface.** `skill_links_create_missing <workflow_dir> <project_dir>`.
  - Stdout: one line per created link. Sets the global `SKILL_LINKS_NOT_CREATED` to the comma-separated names that are missing and were not created (bash 3.2 has no namerefs; a global string matches how `pending-changes.sh` already builds `missing_skills`). Always returns 0, writes nothing to stderr (every mutating command has `2>/dev/null`).
  - Caller contract: `pending-changes.sh` prints the warning line from the module's remaining-missing set, so the warning text, the `, ` separator and the "adopt.sh again" sentence stay byte-identical (S9 and its greps keep working).
- **Decision procedure, in this order, all read-only until the last step.**
  1. Adopted: `readlink <project>/.claude/settings.json` is non-empty and `dirname(dirname(target))`, resolved with `pwd -P` (a relative target is resolved against `<project>/.claude`), equals `workflow_dir` resolved with `pwd -P`. This is the same derivation the hook command uses to find `wf`, so "the hook runs" and "adopted" cannot disagree. Not adopted: create nothing, keep the warning.
  2. `.claude/skills` is not a symlink, and is either absent or a directory. Otherwise create nothing, keep the warning.
  3. Candidates: each `<workflow_dir>/skills/*/` for which `[ -e path ] || [ -L path ]` is false under `.claude/skills/<name>` (a dangling link counts as present for creation, Human decision 1; the warning's own check stays `-e`, so a dangling link keeps appearing in the warning). Real directory, file, foreign link and dangling link are therefore skipped by the same rule, with no separate cases.
  4. Gitignored: `git -C <project> check-ignore -q -- .claude/skills/<name>` per candidate. Exit 0 means ignored; exit 1 (not ignored) or 128 (not a repo, error) means skip and keep the warning. The path is tested **including the skill name**, never `.claude/skills` or `.claude/skills/` alone: the managed block entry `.claude/skills/` is a directory-only pattern, and `check-ignore` on a not-yet-existing path cannot know it is a directory, so the bare directory path reports "not ignored" in exactly the S9 case (absent directory). With a path below it the pattern matches whether or not anything exists. Verified in this repo: both `.claude/skills` and `.claude/skills/x` report ignored, and the per-name form is the one that stays correct when the directory is absent. It also honours the project's own ignore rules, `.git/info/exclude` and a global excludes file, which is the right notion of "ignored" for "no `git status` noise".
  5. `mkdir -p .claude/skills` only if at least one candidate passed step 4, then `ln -s <workflow_dir>/skills/<name> .claude/skills/<name>` per candidate. A failing `mkdir` or `ln` leaves that name in `SKILL_LINKS_NOT_CREATED` and the loop continues (AC4). The link target uses the `workflow_dir` the hook was given, which for a hook that ran is the same checkout `adopt.sh` recorded.
- **Idempotence and upstream removal (AC6).** Only existing `skills/*/` are iterated and nothing is ever removed, so a second run finds no candidates and prints nothing; a skill removed upstream is never created, and its dangling link is `adopt.sh`'s cleanup problem.
- **Fail-open behaviour.** No `git` on `PATH`, a non-repo project, an unreadable `.claude/`, a read-only filesystem: each falls to "keep the warning", exit 0, empty stderr. Cost, accepted: in those cases the hook is advisory, as today.
- **Report line wording (one line per link plus one trailing line).**
  `Created skill link: .claude/skills/<name> -> <workflow_dir>/skills/<name>`
  and, once, after the last created link:
  `New skill links may not be visible to this session; they are available from the next session start.`
  The second line is the answer to Product's open risk (below). Nothing is printed when nothing was created, so a repeat session is silent.
- **Product's open risk: does Claude Code discover a skill linked during SessionStart in the same session? Not established, so the line says "may".** It cannot be settled from this repo's files: skill discovery lives in the Claude Code runtime, and neither the repo nor the hook contract documents when it scans relative to `SessionStart` hooks, or whether it watches a `.claude/skills/` directory that did not exist at launch. The only certain statement is the one the line makes: the next session start has them. A one-time manual probe (create a skill link from a `SessionStart` hook in a throwaway project, ask the session to list its skills) would settle the fact, and QA or the Developer may run it and then tighten the second line to a plain statement; the design does not depend on the answer, since the link on disk is correct either way. The line must not promise same-session availability.
- **Test Seam.** The Seam is the file system plus `git`, entered at `pending-changes.sh <project>` (the module's only caller, so tests cross the same Interface as the hook; do not source the lib in tests). A fake adopted project is built with the existing helpers, as S9 already does: `sandbox_copy_repo` (a throwaway copy of the workflow whose `skills/` the test controls), `fresh_project`, then `adopt.sh <project>` with `SPEC_DRIVEN_GUARDRAILS_DIR` pointing at the copy. `adopt.sh` makes `.claude/settings.json` a symlink into the copy and writes the managed ignore block, so the "adopted" and "gitignored" preconditions come from the real installer, not a hand-built imitation. The stale states are then made by changing the copy afterwards: add `skills/<name>/` directories after the adoption (missing links), `rm -rf` the project's `.claude/skills` (absent directory, S9's case), pre-create a real directory, file, foreign link or dangling link at one name (AC3), `chmod a-w` the `.claude` directory (AC4; skip the case when running as root), repoint `settings.json` or delete the ignore block from `.gitignore` (AC5), replace `.claude/skills` by a symlink or a file (AC5). Assertions: stdout lines, remaining warning, `readlink` values, `git -C <project> status --porcelain` unchanged, exit 0, stderr empty (run with `2>"$file"` and assert the file is empty, since the hook itself discards stderr). Two real adapters for the Seam are the real `git` and the real file system, so no fake `git` is introduced.
- **Spec amendments for Product (flagged, not written here).**
  - **S9** (`TEST-SCENARIOS.md`, `Covers: F6`): "the hook reports that `adopt.sh` needs to run again" is no longer true for an adopted, ignored project; rewrite S9 as create-and-report (AC1, AC2) and move the remaining warning into its own scenarios (not adopted, not ignored, `.claude/skills` a symlink or file, existing path of each kind, read-only). Keep `test/cases/s9_outdated_adoption.sh`'s fixture idea but note its current setup stops being a warning case: it adopts with `skills/` removed, adds skills, and expects the warning, so the new S9 fixture must either break the ignore precondition for the warning half or assert the created links instead. QA owns the test, Product the scenario text.
  - **PRD F9**: replace "new skills only arrive when `adopt.sh` is re-run" with: `adopt.sh` installs, refreshes and cleans up; the SessionStart hook additionally creates links that are missing, in an adopted project whose `.claude/skills/` is gitignored, and never overwrites or removes any path. Also add the report line's "next session" caveat.
  - **F6** text if it repeats the old warning behaviour; check `CHANGES.md`/CHANGELOG for a hook-change entry like A20 (the hook change ships through the symlinked checkout; no adoption question, so no `CHANGES.md` entry is proposed, a `CHANGELOG.md` line is).
  - The stale NOTE comment above the block in `pending-changes.sh` is rewritten by the Developer (AC7).
- **Effort.** Architect: this entry, about 1 hour. Downstream: QA about 2 hours (about 8 scenarios, most reuse S9's setup); Developer about 2 hours (one lib, a 5-line call-site change, comment fix, `./check`); spec edits about 1 hour. Total S.
- **Risks.** (R1) `git check-ignore` semantics for a directory-only pattern with an absent directory: handled by the per-name path; QA must include the absent-directory case so a regression to the bare path is caught. (R2) macOS bash 3.2: no namerefs, no `${var,,}`; the global string covers it. (R3) A project whose `.gitignore` ignores `.claude/skills/` but whose `.claude/skills` content is tracked from before: a new link is untracked and ignored, so no noise, but `adopt.sh`'s untracking is not run; unchanged from today. (R4) Codex is out of scope (#507): the module takes the workflow and project directories only and knows nothing about Claude's settings except the adoption signal in step 1, so #507 will need its own adoption signal (its own installed link), not a reuse of step 1. (R5) Report-line wording must not claim same-session availability.
- **Violated when:** the hook overwrites, removes or repoints any existing path; creates anything in a project whose settings link does not point into this checkout; creates a link in a non-ignored `.claude/skills`; prints to stderr or exits non-zero; or `adopt.sh` and the hook disagree on the link form.

### A46 — Reminder after a main merge; Claude hook and Codex instruction coverage (#500, #561)

- **#561 amendment (2026-10-25, supersedes the stop).** TiesL decided that a merge into `main` no longer ends the session's work. The hook prints the decided reminder as a PostToolUse `systemMessage` (the documented field shown to the user) and emits no `continue` or `stopReason`; work continues in the same turn. The shared rules "run each merge in a distinct tool call" and "only the final result and fresh-context prompt is allowed" are dropped: they existed only to make the stop effective. Codex follows by instruction: it gives the reminder after a confirmed main merge and does not end the turn for it. Unchanged: every successful merge into `main` (any head) reminds; a merge into `release/*` gives no reminder; tag commands and publication are not detected; failed, queued-only and uncertain results give no reminder; every path fails open with exit 0. The 2026-10-21 live Codex observations describe the removed stop and are kept as history only (S363). Text below that described the stop is rewritten; this bullet is the record of the change.

- **Authority and outcome.** Issue #500 AC1–AC8, PRD F56 and human
  decisions 1–8 govern this design. Decision 8 (2026-10-20) supersedes
  the tag-detection parts of decisions 4–7 and of this entry's earlier
  versions. A successful agent-run merge into `main` gives the
  fresh-context reminder, whatever the head branch, including a `release/*`
  head; since #561 it does not end autonomous work. A merge
  into `release/*` continues the epic without a reminder. Nothing detects,
  tracks or waits for tags in either runtime, and tag publication causes
  no stop or prompt. Every reminder carries a short tag note,
  because neither runtime knows whether a release is being tagged. The
  maintainer judges when to reset context, as they judge the merge
  itself. Context
  reset is the maintainer's action, never automatic.

- **Decided wording.** The tag note has the same meaning as decision 8
  and is shorter than its sentence:
  - Claude `systemMessage`: "Merged to main. Type /clear before the next work
    item; if you are tagging a release, tag it first."
  - Codex CLI: "Merged to main. Use /clear or /new before the next work
    item; if you are tagging a release, tag it first."
  - Codex desktop: "Merged to main. Start a New chat before the next
    work item; if you are tagging a release, tag it first."

  If the Codex surface cannot be established, give both labelled actions
  rather than guess. The note appears on every main-merge reminder,
  including non-release ones.

- **Codex feasibility, established before Implementation (2026-10-20).**
  The installed adapter supplies generated instructions, skill/source links
  and native Git hooks. `lib/codex-adoption.py` installs no runtime hook or
  Codex configuration. Its inventory and `session-context.sh --runtime codex`
  correctly report `runtime-hooks: not-installed`. The locally available
  binary reports `codex-cli 0.163.0`: a version observation, not a live
  stop or reset observation. (Background for #500's stop:)
  [Official Hooks documentation](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/hooks)
  describes `PostToolUse` feedback semantics: `continue: false` replaces
  the tool result and permits model continuation. Wiring Claude JSON into a
  Codex hook would therefore not prove the requested stop. #500 uses the
  existing instruction-based adapter. After confirming the merge, Codex
  gives the decided reminder in its response and may continue requested
  work. This is instruction following with no mechanical guarantee. Hook
  installation remains separate work (#544), and is neither required nor
  silently claimed here.

- **Codex Interface and integration.** Put the completion rule in canonical
  `policy/WORKFLOW.md` after the merge step. Put runtime-specific reset
  wording in `adapters/claude/INSTRUCTIONS.md` and
  `adapters/codex/INSTRUCTIONS.md`. Then regenerate `WORKFLOW.md` and
  `adapters/codex/AGENTS.md`. Step 5 names the PR:
  `gh pr merge <n> --squash --delete-branch`.

  Codex identifies the PR number and repository before a merge that may
  delete the branch. Afterwards it confirms `state == MERGED` and base
  `main` using that saved identity. A queued `--auto` result is
  insufficient. Failed or uncertain results give no reminder.

  Judge merge success from the completed merge result. Do required durable
  reporting before the merge. (#561 dropped the distinct-call and
  only-continuation rules.)

  No new polling loop, persistent latch, background process or
  context-clear shell command is introduced.
  [CLI commands](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/developer-commands?surface=cli)
  documents fresh-chat `/clear` and `/new`; a terminal clear does not reset
  the chat, and both require the current task to finish.
  [Desktop commands](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/reference/commands)
  documents New chat (`Cmd+N` on macOS, `Ctrl+N` on Windows/Linux).

  Re-align `skills/release-branch-workflow/SKILL.md`. After a release
  branch's merge into `main` the reminder is given, and tagging is
  a maintainer-requested follow-up, which may run before `/clear`. Remove
  the "tag is the sole continuation, then stop" ordering.

- **Claude Module and Interface.** Add one executable
  `hooks/stop-after-completion` (Python 3 is already a hook dependency).
  Register it synchronously alongside `push-after-commit` under Bash
  `PostToolUse` in `settings/session-hooks.json`, using the existing
  settings-link-to-source resolution.

  Its Interface is hook JSON on stdin, JSON or empty stdout, and exit 0 on
  all advisory or uncertain paths. It performs read-only subprocess lookups
  with argument arrays, bounded timeouts and no `eval` or shell execution
  of input. Malformed JSON, the wrong event or tool, interrupted or
  background-incomplete calls, and unreadable quoting produce no reminder. The
  real [Claude hook contract](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks)
  supplies PostToolUse after successful tools; failure is a different event.
  Do not invent a portable `tool_response.exit_code` field.

  On a qualifying merge, output exactly one JSON object
  `{"systemMessage": "<decided Claude wording>"}`: no `continue`, no
  `stopReason`, no `additionalContext`. `additionalContext` would put "Type
  /clear" into Claude's context and invite the model to halt by itself, which
  would bring back the ordering #561 removes. There is no release-specific `additionalContext`
  output, no tag-form recognition and no local tag-ref resolution. Any
  command that is not a recognised merge, tag commands included, makes
  zero `gh` calls and produces no output.

- **Command interpretation and success evidence.** Reuse command reading
  in `hooks/read-command.py` rather than copy shell parsing or change the
  guard's existing stream Interface. Keep control-operator information
  while judging execution, not just a bag of matching words.

  Recognise actual `gh pr merge` command positions: an explicit
  number/URL/branch or an omitted current-PR target, value-taking flags, and
  `-R`/`--repo` in their supported positions. Query
  `gh pr view [target] --json baseRefName,state` (add `headRefName` only
  for the reflog fallback below), forwarding repository selection. Require
  exact `MERGED` and base `main`. The head no longer matters. Bound lookup
  latency and fail open on errors, malformed output or ambiguity.

  Success is proved only where the shell structure entails that the call's
  success means the command's success: standalone, an all-success `&&`
  chain, or a final command after `;` whose result is the call's result. A
  masked failure (`|| true`, pipeline status, an earlier semicolon segment)
  or a conditional/skipped occurrence must not be turned into success by
  matching text or by finding an old merged PR. Treat an unprovable
  occurrence as uncertain, and process any occurrence that can be proved
  separately.

  No parser promises to interpret arbitrary shell programs, aliases,
  substitutions, wrappers or scripts. Variable expansion (`$VAR`, `${VAR}`, `$1`)
  in the PR target or the `--repo` value is uncertain like a substitution: the
  hook does not expand it, makes no lookup with the unexpanded text, and judges
  only those two words, so a `$` elsewhere in the command does not matter.
  Commands already run in the same Bash
  invocation are unaffected; since #561 that is harmless, so no separate-call
  rule is needed. Web-UI and subagent
  merges stay excluded by human decision.

- **Omitted-target merge (review round 1, `completion-canonical-merge-no-stop`).**
  `gh pr merge --squash --delete-branch` with no target, run from the head
  branch, checks out another branch and deletes the head before PostToolUse
  runs. Two measures cover this, and both are required.

  1. **Explicit number.** Canonical step 5 names the PR (above), so both
     runtimes use the explicit-target path.
  2. **Reflog fallback.** AC4 still covers the omitted form, so the hook
     has a fallback for it. The fallback applies only when the parsed merge
     has no target, carries `-d`/`--delete-branch`, and the post-call HEAD
     is not a `feature/`/`fix/`/`release/` branch.

     Read the two newest HEAD reflog subjects
     (`git reflog -2 --format=%gs HEAD`). Real `gh pr merge -d` (verified
     against gh 2.102.0 and this repository's own reflog on the merges of
     #516, #505 and #548) checks out the base, then runs
     `git pull --ff-only <remote> <base>`, and only then deletes the head.
     After a squash merge the local base is behind, so the pull
     fast-forwards and writes its own entry after the checkout. The rule
     therefore accepts exactly these two shapes, newest first:

     - `pull --ff-only <remote> <current>: Fast-forward`, then
       `checkout: moving from <B> to <current>`;
     - `checkout: moving from <B> to <current>` as the newest entry (the
       pull failed or had nothing to fast-forward, so it wrote nothing).

     `<remote>` is one word without spaces. Any other newest entry (a
     commit, a reset, a second checkout, a pull of a different branch, a
     pull that did not fast-forward) makes the occurrence uncertain. Only
     this one pull entry may be skipped, and only directly above the
     checkout. `<B>` must match `feature/`/`fix/`/`release/`, and
     `refs/heads/<B>` must no longer exist. Then look up `gh pr view <B>`
     with repository forwarding, and require `MERGED`, base `main` and
     `headRefName == <B>`.

     Any mismatch, missing entry, surviving branch or lookup failure stays
     uncertain: exit 0 with no reminder. Never fall back to the new current
     branch's PR.

  **Review round 2 amendment (`completion-reflog-fallback-masked-by-gh-pull`,
  `completion-reflog-fallback-defeated-by-gh-pull`).** The round-1 rule
  required the checkout to be the newest entry. That premise was wrong
  about real `gh`: the pull entry always sits above it, so the fallback
  never fired and the omitted form failed open. The S359 fixture modelled
  checkout plus delete without the pull, so its positive case proved a
  state that real `gh` does not produce. Confirmed as a design defect and
  corrected above. Alternatives weighed in round 2:
  - Drop the fallback and document the omitted form as uncertain. It is
    the simplest change, but AC4 lists "current-branch omission" among
    the merge forms that receive AC1 behaviour, and the decision-8
    reading keeps the omitted form in scope. Choosing it would override
    AC wording, so it is not open to Planning.
  - Take the newest `checkout: moving from …` entry anywhere in the
    reflog. It is looser than needed: a stale checkout from hours earlier
    could name a branch that happens to be merged. The two-entry bound
    ties recognition to the command that just ran.
  - Query `gh` for the most recently merged PR, or the current user's
    last merged PR. It cannot tell this merge from another session's or a
    web-UI merge, and adds a broader `gh` call.
  - A PreToolUse state file recording the branch before the merge.
    Rejected in round 1 for the same reason as below (second event,
    persistent latch).
  The chosen change keeps one Module, one Interface and the same lookups;
  it widens one string check to one optional predecessor entry.

  Two alternatives were rejected:
  - Parsing `gh`'s merge message: it is printed only on a TTY.
  - A PreToolUse state file: it adds a second event and a persistent latch,
    and the reflog already is Git's durable record of the pre-merge branch
    (deletion test).

  The residual risk is a stale reflog entry together with a successful
  omitted-target merge run from a non-eligible branch. It is accepted: it
  reminds only when `<B>`'s PR really is MERGED into `main`.

- **Output redirections (review round 1, `completion-merge-redirection-uncertain`).**
  An output redirection does not change a simple command's exit status: if
  the redirection fails, the command does not run and the call fails. These
  forms therefore keep the success proof intact:
  - `N>&M` with digit fds;
  - `>`, `>>`, `2>` and `&>`, each to one literal (unexpanded) target word.

  The shared reader classifies them as redirection records attached to the
  simple command. A redirection record is not a word (no extra target) and
  not a control operator (the `&` in `>&` is not background). The legacy
  `tokenize`/stream projection stays byte-identical, so the guard is
  unaffected.

  Any other redirection stays uncertain: input, here-string, process
  substitution, expanded target, or fd close. A pipeline stays uncertain,
  because without `pipefail` its status is the last command's. README and
  CHANGELOG coverage statements name the remaining uncertain forms (pipes,
  unsupported redirections, wrappers) instead of claiming that every main
  merge reminds.

- **Quote provenance (finding `completion-token-quote-provenance`).**
  The old decoded `list[str]` tokenizer Interface is insufficient for
  completion evidence, because an unquoted shell separator and a quoted
  argument can both decode to `;`. `echo ";" "gh" "pr" "merge" "500"`
  only prints text, and finding an old MERGED PR must never promote those
  arguments into an executed command.

  Keep lexical provenance until command positions and success entailment
  have been decided. The shared reader provides typed lexical records that
  distinguish a word from an actual control operator (and from a
  redirection record, above). Each word carries its decoded literal value
  and enough source/quote/escape provenance to tell literal content from
  unsupported active shell syntax.

  Only unquoted, unescaped operator syntax can divide commands or form
  `&&`/`||`/pipeline relations; never infer an operator from a decoded
  value. Quoted, escaped and concatenated word fragments remain one word,
  even when their value equals punctuation. Words become command candidates
  only at a syntactically established command position. Quoting a literal
  command word (for example `"gh" pr merge 500`) does not by itself make
  that word data; its position decides that. Arguments to `echo`, `printf`
  and other commands never become command positions by resemblance.

  Put this lexical knowledge in the existing reader Module, with a
  provenance-preserving entry used by the completion Module. Its existing
  `tokenize` caller contract and `c`/`t`/`e` NUL stream remain compatible:
  derive their decoded projection from the same lexical reading instead of
  maintaining a second shell lexer. Developer may choose the private record
  representation. Word/operator/redirection kind and literal-versus-active
  provenance are required semantics, not optional heuristics. Do not repair
  this by rejecting all quoting or all compound commands, by stripping
  quotes before scanning, or by replacing quoted punctuation with guessed
  separators.

  This is a bounded shell recognizer, not an interpreter:
  - Escapes and quotes are handled during lexing, including escaped
    punctuation and backslash-newline line continuation (implemented in
    round 2; legacy guard stream unchanged).
  - Comments and heredoc bodies are data, never command evidence.
  - Active expansions, command/process substitutions, unsupported
    redirections or control syntax that the recognizer cannot safely
    classify make the affected occurrence uncertain.
  - Reject ambiguity before querying `gh`, and never execute input to
    resolve it.

- **Depth, Seam, Leverage and Locality.** One completion Module hides
  merge recognition, result confirmation and Claude output behind one
  executable Interface. The Seam for QA is that executable plus stdin, a
  temporary repository, and PATH-provided `gh` fixtures, exactly as runtime
  callers enter it.

  Shared provenance-aware reading supplies Depth, Leverage and Locality:
  deleting it would spread quote/operator/redirection rules across the
  guard and completion callers. Its legacy stream and its completion
  reading are two real callers, so the two-adapters rule justifies this
  existing reader Seam. It does not justify a new plugin lexer or parser
  framework.

  Deletion test: deleting the completion Module would put the same
  recognition and result rules into settings commands and tests, so it
  earns its place. Dropping tag detection (decision 8) removes a whole
  recognition branch and its local-ref lookups. The Module gets shallower
  in behaviour without losing its reason to exist.

  Do not invent a common runtime hook abstraction: the two real adapters
  differ in enforcement and do not satisfy one completion Interface.

- **QA handoff.** Demonstrate red before green through the executable Seam:
  - AC1 for any head, including `release/*`, with the exact tag-note
    `systemMessage` and no `continue`/`stopReason`, plus a mutant check that goes red if `continue: false` returns. AC2 release-base continuation.
  - AC3 failed/queued/timeout/malformed.
  - AC4: unrelated commands with zero `gh` invocations; explicit, URL,
    branch and omitted targets; repository flags; the
    branch-switching/deleting omitted-target fixture, which must reproduce
    real `gh`'s checkout, `pull --ff-only` fast-forward from a bare remote
    holding the squash commit, then delete; a checkout-only variant (pull
    wrote nothing); and negatives (surviving branch, newest entry neither
    the pull nor the checkout, a pull entry for a branch other than the
    current one, a pull entry above a non-checkout entry, no
    `--delete-branch`, mismatched head); compound `&&` and semicolon-final success;
    masked/skipped/pipeline negatives; the quote-provenance matrix; and
    redirection positives (`2>&1`, `>/dev/null`) and pipe negatives.
  - AC5: tag commands and tag publication (`git push <remote> <tag>`,
    `--tags`, `--follow-tags`, `gh release create`) produce no output and
    zero `gh` calls.

  Fake `gh` asserts target/repository and returns states. Test the
  generated/adopted instructions through the real generator and
  `adopt.sh --runtime codex` in a throwaway project. Assert both CLI and
  desktop wording with the tag note, untouched user config and a truthful
  coverage inventory. Do not source private functions. Script tests cannot
  establish live behaviour.

  For the #500 live Codex evidence (historical since #561): record the exact surface/version and loaded
  instructions. Use a PATH fake `gh` and a local bare remote, and label the
  simulated remote state. Observe that a subsequent sentinel action does
  not run after a main merge (any head), and does run after a release-base
  merge and after negatives. Record unavailable surfaces and unperformed
  resets as unverified, never as passes. Evidence gathered under the old
  tag design does not count for the tag-note wording. Live Claude hook
  execution remains unverified in this Codex environment. The retained runs observed the removed stop; #561 requires no new live run and claims none.

- **Adoption and notice.** Per A20, the existing settings symlink delivers
  the Claude hook. The Codex managed AGENTS block updates through the
  normal `adopt.sh --runtime codex` rerun, followed by a fresh session.
  Include a `CHANGELOG.md` notice and a README/runtime-dry-run coverage
  update.

  No new per-project option, configuration ownership or meaning-version
  change is proposed. The lifecycle rule is unconditional, so no
  `CHANGES.md` question or `WORKFLOW-ADOPTION.md` answer is required. Keep
  `runtime-hooks: not-installed` truthful. No change to ORCHESTRATOR core
  is needed.

- **Estimate and open decisions.** Architect share: about half a day for
  the original design, ~1.5h for round 1, ~1h for the decision-8
  rewrite and ~45min for the round-2 reflog amendment (Implementation/QA
  delta: XS, one hook condition plus the fixture and negatives). Decision 8 reduces Implementation/QA work: removing tag code
  and scenarios is offset by the reflog fallback and redirection records,
  for a net S on top of the existing M. Codex parity for the tag note is
  Product's inference from decision 7, and the maintainer may veto it.
  Automatic clearing is not
  established; requiring it would reopen human scope.

### A47 — Opt-in Codex merge interception; verified hook contract (#544)

- **Authority.** [#516 Human decision 4](https://github.com/TiesL/spec-driven-guardrails/issues/516#issuecomment-6286538090)
  authorizes this separate opt-in, implementing #544 AC1–AC7. A39's promise
  not to touch Codex configuration remains the default. Only an explicit
  `adopt.sh --runtime codex --hooks [project]` grants ownership of one hook
  definition in project `.codex/hooks.json`; trust, permissions, user config,
  plugins and unrelated hooks remain project/user-owned. This is a capability
  opt-in, not mandatory new workflow policy; no CHANGES meaning bump is needed.
- **Module / Interface.** Extend the existing Codex adoption Module
  (`lib/codex-adoption.py` behind `adopt.sh`), retaining its complete ownership
  preflight before writes. `--hooks` is Codex-only; repeated/invalid combinations
  fail with exit 2 before writes. A run without `--hooks` neither creates nor
  rewrites hook configuration, including after an earlier opted-in run; absence
  of the flag is not an uninstall request. Status always inspects actual state.
- **Coexistence.** Parse the regular project hooks JSON, preserve unrelated keys
  and hook definitions semantically, and append exactly one dedicated matcher
  group identified through local provenance plus its exact managed definition.
  Update only a definition matching its recorded previous value; duplicates,
  malformed JSON/shapes, foreign edits to recorded ownership, unsafe parents or
  symlinks conflict before any writes. Preserve `.codex/config.toml` byte for
  byte, including inline hooks; do not consolidate user hooks or change global
  configuration. Record opt-in/definition ownership in the existing local
  installation record with explicit backward-compatible version handling.
  A source template supplies the canonical definition, not a whole-file symlink.
  Resolve the guard from the adopted project's `.guardrails/source` using a
  safely quoted project-root path, including calls launched in subdirectories.
  The #594 amendment below supersedes this source-path resolution for the
  installed command and extends the provenance and status rules for bundles.
- **Guard Interface.** AC4 requires all non-merge Bash commands to remain usable.
  Wiring the full guard unchanged would also enforce destructive-Git and
  issue-first rules. Add an explicit `--merge-only` invocation mode to the
  existing guard Module: reuse its token reader, segment/cwd handling and merge
  decision implementation, but skip non-merge judgments in that mode. Its
  no-argument Claude and preflight behavior remains unchanged. Do not duplicate
  command parsing or the merge checks in a Codex-specific guard. The external
  Seam remains hook stdin plus exit status/stderr; Claude and Codex are two real
  adapters, satisfying the two-adapters rule. This preserves Depth, Leverage
  and Locality: deleting the shared Module would distribute tokenization and
  merge policy among adapters (the deletion test). No new dispatch framework.
- **Status semantics.** `runtime-hooks: installed` means the exact managed
  definition and its reachable target are structurally present; also print
  `scope: Bash merge interception; activation: unverified`. Missing/not opted-in
  reports `runtime-hooks: not-installed`; edited/duplicate/broken definitions
  report conflict/stale, never installed. Status without `--hooks` must still
  detect an earlier install. Retain existing status exit meanings (0 current,
  1 stale/conflict, 2 invalid/unreadable). Installation does not establish
  effective activation: project trust, exact-hook review, disabled hooks,
  administrator policy and runtime support may suppress execution. Adoption
  never grants trust or bypasses review. Clarify generated Codex instructions,
  session-context diagnostics and README so default absence and optional
  structural installation are both truthful; voluntary merge-preflight remains
  required whenever interception is unavailable. No SessionStart/PostToolUse/
  SessionEnd automation is implied.
- **Live prerequisite — SATISFIED (2026-10-21).** In the direct session
  identified by the maintainer as Codex CLI, after reviewing and trusting the
  exact project hook `python3 /private/tmp/codex-544-probe/probe.py`, the hook
  captured real callbacks for both marker commands. The project
  `.codex/hooks.json` contained `hooks.PreToolUse` with matcher `Bash` and a
  command hook invoking that script. Captured JSON contains
  `hook_event_name: PreToolUse`, `tool_name: Bash`,
  `tool_input.command: printf PROBE_DENY_544` (then `printf PROBE_ALLOW_544`),
  and `cwd: /private/tmp/codex-544-probe`; session/turn/transcript/model/
  permission/tool-use metadata are also present. The script's exit 2 plus
  `PROBE_544_REFUSAL` on stderr produced `Command blocked by PreToolUse hook:
  PROBE_544_REFUSAL` before execution. Exit 0 with no output allowed the other
  command, which printed `PROBE_ALLOW_544` and exited 0. Use this stdin JSON
  and exit-status/stderr contract; no response JSON is required for these
  allow/deny outcomes.
- **Evidence and limits.** The captured event's transcript is the local rollout
  ending `01a15d4d-f8a8-73c0-ac43-3e6a55b3290c.jsonl`; its command results
  independently confirm the refusal and allowed output. Metadata records
  `cli_version: 0.163.0`, `originator: Codex Desktop`, `source: vscode` and
  event model `gpt-6-sol`. The surface labels differ from the maintainer's CLI
  description, so this establishes the observed direct-session contract,
  without establishing separate desktop coverage. Desktop remains unverified
  as a separate surface. Earlier nested `codex exec` probes with no callback
  are inconclusive about loading/activation; their cause remains unresolved
  and they do not disprove the captured contract. The synthetic first line in
  `events.jsonl` is a standalone script test, not runtime evidence. No further
  paid live probe is needed for Planning.
- **Activation and fixture contract.** [Official Hooks documentation](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/hooks)
  supplies configuration context; the captured callbacks and tool results
  supply the protocol evidence. Exact-hook review/trust remains a user action;
  installation cannot grant it, and an updated command may need review again.
  Sanitize session identifiers and local paths in committed fixtures while
  retaining event/tool/command/cwd and the observed allow/refuse outcomes.
  Automated coverage must exercise that contract and shared guard refusal
  using fake `gh`, never a real merge. Do not generalize this observation to
  hooks disabled, trust withheld, other versions or independently untested
  surfaces; report those as activation unavailable/unverified.
- **QA handoff.** Cover default no-config writes,
  repeat opt-in without duplicates, preservation of JSON/inline/global hooks,
  owned-definition repair/conflict, unsafe paths, old provenance, subdirectory
  and space-containing project paths, status absent/current/drift/broken,
  captured live event/exit contract, shared guard allow/refuse with fake `gh`,
  non-merge destructive-Git commands passing merge-only mode, and unchanged
  default guard behavior. Include trust withheld/review pending/hooks disabled
  as unavailable activation, not installed enforcement. Automated fixtures
  alone cannot replace the live evidence above. Architect effort: about half a
  day including runtime investigation; overall M remains plausible.
- **Next stage.** Planning is complete. Proceed to QA test strategy/scenarios,
  then Developer implementation under this decision; no product scope change
  or waiver of the live prerequisite is required.

#### A47 amendment — staged guard bundle publication and explicit recovery (#594, PR #600)

- **Authority and numbering.** TiesL accepted the Architect's staged bundle,
  atomic exchange and transaction recommendation in full on 2026-10-30. This
  amends the existing Codex guard decision A47, the highest A-number on this
  branch at c2f218a. It allocates no new number and cannot clash with A48
  planned by #599. PRD F47 and S397-S411 describe the affected behavior;
  Product must update F47 and QA must extend the interruption scenarios.
- **Module / Interface.** Keep publication and recovery in the existing
  Codex adoption Module behind the `adopt.sh` Interface. Its Depth hides the
  transaction at the existing adoption and read-only status Seam, preserving
  Leverage and Locality for callers. A separate transaction framework would
  spread this knowledge across callers rather than pass the deletion test;
  no new Adapter abstraction is justified by the two-adapters rule.
  The installed command targets the real, machine-local directory
  `.codex/sdg-guard/`, containing exactly the seven declared guard files and
  MANIFEST, with source bytes, modes and bundle-relative layout preserved.
  MANIFEST records file sha256 values, modes and source revision. Ownership
  anchors its exact sha256 independently in `.guardrails/installation.json`.
  The bundle stays gitignored; foreign `.codex/` files are preserved. Repeating
  the same complete installation is a no-op. Content refresh reports changed
  files and old/new revisions, retains the command string and does not renew
  hook review/trust. Adoption grants neither trust nor permissions.
- **Publication mechanism and support limit.** Construct and fully verify a
  staging directory on the same filesystem as the active directory, then
  exchange the two real directories atomically. Use macOS `renameatx_np`
  with `RENAME_SWAP`, or Linux `renameat2` with `RENAME_EXCHANGE`. These are
  proposed mechanisms, unverified on this machine; this decision records no
  successful platform probe. Refuse refresh if the platform or filesystem
  cannot supply the exchange, leaving the active bundle unchanged. Never
  fall back to two renames, in-place overwrites or per-file replacement of
  the active bundle: those expose a missing path or mixed generation.
  Check support before starting the transaction where possible; a runtime
  unsupported-exchange error leaves the ready transaction for explicit retry,
  without publishing or silently switching mechanisms.
- **Provenance version 4.** Continue strict reading of versions 1, 2 and 3
  with their existing schemas; explicit bundle adoption upgrades to version 4
  with a reported provenance upgrade. Default adoption and status must not
  upgrade an older bundle record implicitly. Version 4 has exactly the
  version-3 fields `owner`, `version`, `runtime`, `checkout`, `links`,
  `managed_hook`, `guard_bundle`, plus `guard_bundle_transaction`. Preserve
  existing ownership, link and hook validation. Version is the integer 4;
  `guard_bundle` still has exactly `path` and `manifest_sha256`, with path
  `.codex/sdg-guard` and a lowercase 64-hex digest. The transaction is null
  in a complete installation, otherwise an object with exactly `phase`,
  `staging_path`, `old_manifest_sha256` and `new_manifest_sha256`. Both
  digests are lowercase 64-hex strings; the phase is exactly `preparing`,
  `ready` or `cleanup`. The staging path is one reserved project-relative
  sibling of the active directory beneath the real `.codex` directory,
  named `.sdg-guard-stage-` followed by a nonempty ASCII alphanumeric token.
  Reject absolute paths, traversal, alternate spellings, unknown or missing
  fields, wrong types and unknown phases. Bind cleanup and recovery to this
  exact path, never a wildcard or a directory discovered by scanning.
  In `preparing` and `ready`, the committed ownership digest equals the old
  digest; in `cleanup`, it equals the new digest. Reject inconsistent records.
  No-op refresh needs no transaction; equal old/new digests do not authorize
  an ambiguous exchange. Metadata is an authorization anchor, not permission
  to accept arbitrary self-consistent manifests or changed active bytes.
- **State machine and writer serialization.** The refresh states are complete
  old installation, `preparing`, `ready`, exchanged while still `ready`,
  `cleanup`, and complete new installation. Serialize adoption writers
  exclusively from preflight through recovery and final record replacement;
  an accidentally overlapping writer must refuse before writes, including
  unrelated adoption writes. Serialization prevents accidental overlap of
  adoption writers; a same-user process that deliberately forges the
  re-execution handoff is outside the threat model (such a process can already
  edit the installation record, MANIFEST and hooks directly).
  Use serialization released on process termination so an
  interrupted writer does not require unsafe lock-file deletion. Complete
  existing preflight, including unrelated ownership checks, before any write.
  Every installation-record transition uses a complete temporary regular file
  and atomic replacement, so interruption exposes either complete record.
  This is an interrupted-process design; it makes no additional claim about
  power-loss durability of filesystem or storage caches.
- **Preparation and its interruption points.** From the validated old state,
  atomically write the `preparing` record with both digests and the exact
  reserved staging path before constructing staging. If interrupted before
  record replacement, the old record and active bundle remain coherent; after
  replacement, an absent or incomplete stage is authorized preparation data.
  Write the seven files with their original relative names and modes and
  construct MANIFEST there, leaving active contents untouched. Before or
  during those writes, interruption leaves the old executable policy intact.
  On explicit recovery, discard only validated transaction-owned preparation
  data and rebuild; incomplete staging is never an executable generation.
  Refuse unexpected paths and symlinks rather than following them recursively.
- **Readiness and exchange interruption points.** Fully validate staged
  inventory, MANIFEST digest and mode, and each file's bytes and mode against
  the intended new generation before atomically recording `ready`. An
  interruption during that record replacement leaves either `preparing`,
  which can rebuild staging, or `ready`, which requires complete validation
  of both generations before publication. Exchange active and staging once.
  Interruption at the exchange leaves either old-active/new-staged or
  new-active/old-staged, both with complete contents. The `ready` record
  authorizes recognizing either arrangement only by full validation against
  its exact old and new digests. Names or a self-consistent MANIFEST alone
  cannot establish which arrangement exists. Recovery exchanges only the
  former arrangement; it must not exchange the latter back to the old state.
- **Ownership commit and cleanup interruption points.** After validating the
  published new generation, atomically commit its ownership digest together
  with phase `cleanup`. An interruption at that replacement leaves either
  `ready` with new active and complete old staged, or `cleanup` with new
  committed ownership. Only after this commit remove the transaction-owned
  old generation, then atomically clear the transaction to null. During
  cleanup, validate the new active bundle fully and permit only the recorded
  old inventory, matching bytes and modes for entries still present, beneath
  the exact staging path. Missing old entries, including an already removed
  stage, are compatible with interrupted cleanup; changed entries, extra
  paths and symlinks are conflicts. Interruption during deletion therefore
  permits idempotent cleanup without authorizing changes to active contents.
  Interruption while clearing metadata leaves either a resumable `cleanup`
  record or a complete installation. Successful refresh leaves no transient
  staging artifacts, preserving S401's final snapshot.
- **Recovery trigger and validation.** An explicit second
  `adopt.sh --runtime codex --hooks` run authorizes recovery. Reconcile the
  recorded transaction before planning a further refresh, even if current
  source has changed since preparation. Repeat the same validation and
  state transitions on every retry; interruption during recovery has the
  same interpretation as interruption during the original transition.
  Unknown phases, malformed transactions, impossible arrangements and an
  active bundle matching neither authorized generation conflict before
  writes. Existing symlink and tamper refusals remain unchanged, including
  `.codex`, the active bundle, all inner entries and transaction paths; name
  the offending path. Never take over an unrecorded bundle or treat active
  tampering as recoverable just because transaction metadata exists.
  Default adoption and `--status` never recover, remove staging data or clear
  metadata. A pending transaction is preserved rather than overwritten by
  otherwise ordinary adoption work.
- **Status and exit meanings.** For a valid interrupted transaction report
  `recovery pending` and exit 1, preserving its current or stale content
  classification where applicable. Pending recovery is distinct from corrupt
  or tampered contents. Retain current, stale, corrupt and absent states:
  exit 0 requires a complete current installation, including the valid
  default state with no opted-in bundle; stale, conflict and recovery pending
  exit 1; invalid or unreadable input exits 2. A missing owned bundle remains
  an absent conflict, not the valid default absence. Malformed transaction
  provenance is an ownership conflict under the existing record policy.
  Status remains read-only, says `activation: unverified` and directs TiesL
  to perform explicit refresh/recovery outside the sandbox. Neither this
  decision nor structural status proves live protection or activation.
- **Quiescent refresh limit.** TiesL must refresh while no hook is executing
  and prevent hook execution until refresh or recovery completes. Atomic
  exchange guarantees complete published directory contents across process
  interruptions; it does not pin a generation for a concurrently running
  script that later resolves sibling dependencies through the exchanged
  pathname. Writer serialization does not coordinate hook execution. Do not
  claim concurrent hooks are safe. Supporting that requires a separate
  generation-pinning or execution-coordination design.
- **S411 compatibility and QA handoff.** Preserve staging filenames ending
  in each original bundle-relative path under the project's `.codex` so
  S411's `Path.write_bytes` partial-write injector reaches all seven files.
  Do not evade it by changing write primitives or suffixes; do not change
  S411 or its assertions. Each injection must be confirmed, refresh must
  fail, and the installed command must retain the exact missing-review exit
  2, stdout and stderr. Explicit retry must recover to current status with
  the same verdict. S411 covers preparation writes, not all transaction
  transitions. QA must add preparation-record, ready-record, exchange,
  ownership-commit and cleanup interruption cases, interruption during
  recovery, active tampering despite metadata, malformed transactions,
  symlinks, unsupported exchange and overlapping writers. Preserve S397-S410,
  including closure sufficiency/necessity, trust/config limits and parity.
- **Other adopted files.** Most adopted files are symlinks into the SDG
  clone and do not require copied-content refresh. The guard bundle is the
  copy addressed here. Issue templates are `cp -f` copies; their lower-risk
  refresh behavior is outside this decision's scope.
- **Interrupted preparation: rebuild and retarget (accepted by
  TiesL on 2026-10-30 under OR43; spec-visible: yes).** In `preparing` only, discard the
  validated transaction-owned staging data and rebuild from the current
  source instead of retaining a pinned historical source generation. This
  changes documented recovery behavior and the intended digest/source
  provenance that a retry may publish. Keep PRD unchanged
  here; Product owns any resulting spec update. No new status or exit meaning
  is proposed. The existing Module and Interface retain this recovery logic;
  no new external Seam or persisted source snapshot is needed.
  - Validate the old active generation against the committed old digest and
    validate the exact staging path and any preparation entries under the
    existing ownership, inventory and symlink rules before discarding them:
    only regular files at the seven declared relative paths plus MANIFEST and
    their real parent directories are disposable preparation data. Partial
    file bytes are not executable or publication evidence; cleanup of this
    incomplete data needs no historical source bytes. Never require an
    incomplete stage to reconstruct the previously intended
    new bytes. Never discard a `ready` or `cleanup` generation by this rule:
    those phases recover their recorded generations without using current
    source, then plan any further refresh as already specified.
  - Remove preparation data completely before changing the intended digest.
    An interruption before or during removal leaves `preparing`, the unchanged
    old active generation and an absent or partial stage; the next explicit
    retry validates and repeats removal. After removal, determine the current
    source generation, including its MANIFEST, revision, bytes and modes.
    Atomically replace the whole `preparing` record with its new intended
    MANIFEST digest, preserving the old digest and exact staging path, before
    writing any replacement staging contents. An interruption before or during
    replacement leaves either complete record with no stage; either can
    restart this procedure without reconstructing its recorded target.
  - Build and fully verify staging against that newly recorded generation
    before recording `ready`. Interruption while building or validating leaves
    `preparing` and can repeat discard and retarget. If source changes during
    planning/building, do not mark a mismatching or mixed generation ready;
    leave preparation pending for explicit retry. Revision and file evidence
    must describe the same planned source generation. Interruption at the
    `ready` replacement follows the existing two-record outcome: `preparing`
    may rebuild, while `ready` preserves its exact verified generation even
    if source later changes. If the rebuilt target digest equals the old
    digest, verify the old active generation, remove any rebuilt staging
    under the same preparation rules, and atomically clear the transaction
    only after staging is absent instead of exchanging equal generations;
    interruption leaves either resumable preparation or the complete old
    installation. No historical source retention is required by this choice.
- **Cleanup evidence: delete MANIFEST last (internal to the accepted design;
  spec-visible: no).** Preserve the old generation's complete MANIFEST bytes
  and mode at the exact recorded staging path until all other old entries and
  directories have been removed. On each cleanup attempt, fully validate the
  committed new active generation first, then authenticate the remaining old
  MANIFEST against `old_manifest_sha256` and its required mode. Its inventory
  supplies the expected paths, bytes and modes for every remaining old file;
  validate the complete remaining tree before deleting anything. Missing old
  payload entries are allowed, but changed entries, unexpected paths and
  symlinks still conflict. Use individual removals, never an unordered
  recursive deletion that might remove MANIFEST early. No transaction schema,
  copied inventory or transaction-owned trash directory is needed.
  - Before the first deletion, interruption retains the complete old
    generation. During payload-file deletion or removal of empty nested
    directories, interruption retains the authenticated MANIFEST and a subset
    of its inventory. A retry checks remaining files against that evidence
    and resumes; validation does not depend on already deleted payload bytes.
    Remove nested directories bottom-up, rejecting unexpected entries rather
    than following them or deleting them as cleanup data.
  - Only when MANIFEST is the sole remaining entry may it be unlinked, using
    one unlink rather than truncating or rewriting it. Interruption at this
    point leaves either the intact authenticated MANIFEST or an empty staging
    directory. A missing MANIFEST is compatible with cleanup only when that
    exact staging directory is empty or already absent; any other remaining
    entry is a conflict because its validation evidence is gone. The empty
    case needs no old inventory to authorize removal of the recorded empty
    directory. Interruption at that removal leaves an empty or absent stage;
    both permit idempotent completion after validating the new active bundle.
  - Clear the transaction atomically only after staging is absent. An
    interruption leaves either `cleanup` with an absent stage or a complete
    installation, as already specified. This ordering refines internal
    deletion mechanics without changing status, exits, provenance schema or
    documented user recovery behavior. It retains validation evidence for
    every old entry that could still require validation.

### A48 — The emit command takes a role; the dispatch hook checks its role and stage (#599; amends A26 and A41)

- **Why:** on #595 Product was given `--stage Planning`. The emitter
  produced a valid marker for the wrong stage; the missing stage was
  found only at merge. Human decisions D1-D7 on #599 put stage derivation
  in the emitter and role agreement in the dispatch hook.
- **Wrapper (amends A26):** `model-record-emit.sh --role <Role>
  --model <id> [--floor-basis <sentence>]`. The orchestrator fills in
  `--role`; the role supplies its model and, for Reviewer, its
  floor-basis. Exact-case flag values are Product, Architect, QA,
  Developer and Reviewer, mapping to Discovery, Planning, Test,
  Implementation and Review. `Fullstack Developer` is not an emitter
  value, even quoted; the hook alone maps that prefix to Developer.
  `--stage` alone and with `--role` remain accepted indefinitely;
  retirement needs a later decision.
- **Map and refusal order:** `role_stage <role> [<stage>]` in
  `lib/model-record.sh`, next to `marker_emit`, owns the map and the
  mismatch refusal; the wrapper remains a flag parser. Flag-parse errors
  come first, then role/stage disagreement, then `marker_emit`'s own
  reasons. A mismatch returns 2, prints nothing on stdout and one stderr
  line naming the role, supplied stage and expected stage. Matching flags
  produce the same marker as either form alone, in either order.
  Missing, repeated, value-less or unknown flags and invalid role values
  are refused with exit 2, empty stdout and one stderr reason; neither
  role nor stage supplied is also an error. `--role` joins the usage and
  flag-name-as-value checks; `--role=Product` is refused.
- **Planning amendment, option B (PR #601 round 7):** [V] TiesL has
  chosen emit-command lines instead of treating the whole prompt as shell,
  as supplied in this Planning brief. [V] At bc84a4f the implementation's
  `emit_commands` carries quote state across prompt lines, with rollback
  and quote-span exceptions; the supplied round-7 review records prose
  swallowing mid-line commands and a malformed-prose fail-open path.
  These are evidence for replacing that design, not for another quote-span
  exception. [A] The rules below are the recommended replacement contract,
  not a claim that the current hook implements them. Existing wrapper,
  role map and emitter refusal rules above remain unchanged.
- **Module and Interface:** [A] Keep the A41 pure hook core and its stdin
  JSON/public CLI Seam. The line reader and argument reader are private
  implementation details of that Module. No new adapter, parser framework
  or shell dependency. Depth and Leverage come from checking every brief
  through that one Interface; Locality keeps parsing and diagnostics here.
  The deletion test removes the problematic whole-prompt shell machinery
  rather than moving it into callers. The two-adapters rule gives no reason
  to add another Seam.
- **Physical line and continuation contract:** [A] An emit unit starts at
  any physical line containing the existing `EMIT_WORD` script-name match,
  wherever the mention occurs. Ignore text before its first match: bullets,
  numbering, a shell prompt, `cd ... &&`, and prose introductions are not
  shell input. The argument text starts immediately after that match.
  A bare mention contributes no marker command and is not shell-split.
  It cannot open a quote affecting another line. Continuation collection
  is eligible only if the suffix, after leading whitespace, starts with
  a known emitter flag (`--role`, `--stage`, `--model`, `--floor-basis`
  or `--effort`, including equals spellings), or consists only of
  whitespace and the continuation marker. A prose-only mention ending in
  a path backslash therefore cannot absorb the following command. A
  noncontinued suffix containing a guarded role/stage flag is still
  inspected even if introduced by words after the script mention.
  For an eligible command, join the following physical line only when the
  current line ends with an odd run of backslash characters, immediately
  before its line ending. Remove the last backslash and the line ending;
  preserve all other characters and spacing. Normalize CRLF to LF first.
  Trailing spaces after the backslash do not continue. An open quote alone
  never continues a unit. This is a brief-format convention, not a shell
  parser: even a backslash inside single quotes follows this physical rule;
  literal quoted multiline values are outside the supported format.
  Stop at the first line without that continuation marker, at EOF, or at
  32 physical lines total including the starting line. A dangling EOF
  continuation or a request for line 33 is unchecked, never silently
  truncated and validated. Consumed continuation lines are not separately
  scanned; the next unconsumed line starts with fresh state.
- **Bounded reading and failure:** [A] Limit a decoded prompt to 4 Mi
  characters and each unit, including its original continuation text, to
  64 Ki characters. Check limits before shell splitting; do not truncate
  a role to a valid prefix. Read stdin with a 32 MiB byte cap before JSON
  decoding, allowing up to six JSON bytes per decoded character plus
  envelope space; exceeding either input cap is unchecked. These are
  conservative proposed engineering limits, not measured guarantees.
  Scan once in order, without rescanning suffixes of the whole prompt.
  Each unit is split at most once; bounded token storage cannot exceed its
  character bound. No recursion, subprocess, expansion or command execution.
  [V] The settings hook timeout is 10 seconds; timeout allows a dispatch.
  [A] Size/continuation limits, unbalanced quotes, a dangling escape, bad
  JSON/encoding, unreadable policy input and unexpected parser exceptions
  must return exit 0, empty stdout and exactly one bounded stderr diagnostic
  ending in "dispatch allowed unchecked". Do not print prompt contents or
  a traceback. The runtime's timeout itself may prevent this diagnostic;
  it is never evidence of successful validation. Guard the complete core
  entry path, including unit collection, against ordinary exceptions so
  malformed input cannot crash a dispatch. No broad catch converts an
  intentional exit-2 denial to allow. A malformed relevant unit makes the
  entire dispatch unchecked, even beside an otherwise denying unit, as
  the existing malformed-input policy does; there is no partial success.
- **Argument reader:** [A] Use a bounded shlex-style split of a relevant
  unit's argument text only, with POSIX single/double quotes, adjacent
  quoted pieces and backslash escapes. Retain decoded words and their raw
  spellings for the legacy stage reader. Whitespace separates words;
  unquoted semicolon, comma, parentheses, ampersand, pipe and angle brackets
  separate words too, preserving existing terminator controls. They do
  not execute anything or stop the scan of later flags on that unit.
  An unquoted hash at a word start after unescaped whitespace starts a
  comment through the end of its physical line; backslash-escaped whitespace
  is part of the shell word, not a word separator, so a hash after it does
  not start a comment. A comment apostrophe never opens a quote or
  enables continuation; remove that comment before testing continuation.
  Inline command wrappers are presentation: if the script's pathname has
  an immediately preceding single quote, double quote or backtick and the
  last non-whitespace character of the unit is the same character, remove
  that one outer pair before splitting. Other quotes remain argument
  syntax; unmatched wrappers use the malformed-input diagnostic.
  Backticks inside arguments remain literal characters. Unknown words
  are ignored; known flag values are consumed as whole words, so text
  such as `--model "x --role Architect"` is not another role flag.
  A second script mention on the same unit does not reset parsing; later
  top-level flags are still inspected. Real briefs should put each command
  on its own line and avoid explanatory prose after its arguments.
- **Flags, detection and agreement:** [A] A prefix line still detects a
  role dispatch. Without one, any emit unit with the existing guarded
  role/stage flag spelling also detects it, including mid-line and fenced
  commands; `--roles` and `--role=Product` alone still do not detect one.
  Bare mention lines without those spellings are skipped before splitting.
  Within parsed units, read every top-level `--role` and its next complete
  decoded word. Another known flag is not a role value: record the missing
  role value and inspect that next flag independently. Only literal spaces
  between role flag and value qualify
  for the existing recognized role form; tab-separated roles remain an
  explicitly documented unsupported spelling. Missing values, invalid
  complete values and equals-role forms cannot supply a valid role and,
  when a prefix exists, cannot be masked by a matching command elsewhere.
  Repeated role/stage occurrences are all checked, with no last-wins rule;
  duplicate matching flags may pass this shape hook but the emitter still
  rejects duplicates. Read `--stage` with the unchanged `STAGE_FLAG` on
  its raw flag/value spelling, only at top-level flag positions, preserving
  its current quoted-prefix and equals-stage recognition gaps. Do not
  accidentally tighten stage parsing by applying decoded-role equality
  to it. Consume `--model`, `--floor-basis` and legacy `--effort` values as
  complete words to avoid finding flags inside them. Equals-value spellings
  of those non-role flags are opaque words too. A unit's `--model` value
  is not compared with the dispatch tool's model: the existing `model`
  check still requires a nonblank string in `tool_input.model` only.
  `marker-command` needs at least one valid role or legacy stage form.
  With a valid prefix, `role-stage` checks all recognized role/stage
  occurrences across all parsed units against its mapped role/stage;
  any disagreement fails, including contradictory flags on one unit.
  Without a prefix this cross-check is inapplicable and OR8 applies.
  Exit 2, empty stdout, each mapped core rule line once, then AVOID;
  `marker-command` and `role-stage` still map to OR31. OR31's current
  text and inventory mapping stay unchanged in this amendment.
- **Prose, fences and accepted limits:** [A] Prose, apostrophes and quotes
  on other physical lines have no shell meaning and cannot swallow or
  leak into a unit. On an emit unit, only the suffix described above is
  parsed; an apostrophe in trailing explanatory prose can therefore make
  that unit unchecked. Fences, quoted examples and prose introductions
  do not exempt emit units: a mismatching example still denies. A quoted
  value containing a later emit-line mention is an accepted cost of option
  B, not a reason to restore cross-line quote tracking: without explicit
  continuations the opening line is malformed/unchecked and later
  unconsumed emit lines are independent. With explicit continuations a
  quoted script mention may be consumed as value text. No correctness
  claim is made for literal quoted multiline values, here-documents,
  dollar-quote/localized-quote spellings, parameter expansion, command
  substitution, shell evaluation or commands embedded inside a quoted
  shell-program argument. Shell-like words are read literally; neither
  expansion nor Bash equivalence is promised. Per the temporary panel
  decision (2026-10-30, vote 2-1), four role spellings are denied and
  unsupported: dollar-single-quote Product, dollar-double-quote Product,
  Product followed by an empty command substitution, and a tab between
  flag and value. Keep observation coverage for these spellings.
  The quoted OR31 text goes unchecked, and a prose mention with a guarded
  flag spelling and no ROLE SESSION line is denied, both by design.
  A malformed relevant unit or resource cap
  can bypass all checks with a visible unchecked diagnostic; this is the
  existing fail-open trade-off, not a security enforcement guarantee.
- **Removed and retained:** [A] Remove `emit_commands`' whole-prompt shell
  tokenizer, quote-span lookahead, `EMIT_LINE` exceptions, `dq_dead`,
  rollback bookkeeping and whole-prompt word-start collection. Do not
  preserve an unused alternate tokenizer. Replace the custom unbounded
  role-word scan with the bounded unit reader above. Keep the single
  (prefix name, flag name, stage) tuple, `--list-roles`, `STAGE_FLAG`,
  `--list-checks`, `--print-contract`, rule-line lookup, fail-open notes,
  prefix/no-fork checks and Reviewer PR/SHA/gate searches on raw prompt
  text. Per the temporary panel decision (2026-10-30, vote 2-1),
  `hooks/agent-dispatch.py --list-roles` outputs three tab-separated fields
  per line: prefix name (which may contain a space), flag name, then stage.
  The hook's join changes from one space to one tab; drift test S418
  parses by tab and pins this output contract. The wrapper and
  `lib/model-record.sh` do not change for option B.
- **Product handoff, F40 wording (proposal only):** [V] The current text
  says: "The dispatch hook denies a prompt whose emit role or stage does
  not match its `ROLE SESSION:` role, including an old prompt that
  supplies only a stage." [A] Replace with: "The dispatch hook checks
  lines mentioning model-record-emit.sh and their explicitly continued
  lines within A48's bounds. Within this supported brief format, a parsed
  emit role or legacy stage that disagrees with the ROLE SESSION role
  denies the dispatch, including a stage-only command. Prose outside
  those lines is not shell input. Quoted examples and fenced commands
  are checked too. Literal quoted multiline values and shell evaluation
  are outside this check. Malformed or over-limit input allows the
  dispatch with an unchecked diagnostic under the existing fail-open
  policy." Add after the instruction to put the command in every prompt:
  "Put the command on one physical line, or use explicit trailing
  backslash continuations within A48's limits." Clarify F40's mechanical
  verification paragraph that agreement is verified only for this format,
  not for every shell-equivalent prompt. Product owns these PRD edits;
  this Planning step edits ARCHITECTURE.md only.
- **QA handoff, existing cases:** [V] S412 currently accumulates round-2
  through round-6 dispatch expectations in fixture functions `dispatch`,
  `round3_dispatch`, `round4_dispatch`, `round5_dispatch` and
  `round6_dispatch`. [A] No whole scenario S412-S419 is removed.
  In S412, retire the round-3 literal-newline quoted-role denial oracles:
  without explicit continuation those opening units are now malformed
  and unchecked. Retire the entire round-5 648-case hook-verdict matrix
  in `round5_dispatch`, which requires literal newlines inside quotes to
  retain following flags as shell argv. Keep its emitter argv/refusal
  coverage separately if useful; the emitter contract did not change.
  Retire the same whole-shell expectations in round-6
  `round6_quoted_apostrophes`; replace them with format-limit checks.
  Replace the million-character-role effective-denial oracle with a fast
  unchecked-size diagnostic, and retain the million-character ordinary

  adjacent quote/escape checks, ordinary malformed-input diagnostic,
  role/stage terminators and wrappers, role-only and detection controls,
  and the one/three-line explicit-continuation round-4 controls. Keep the

  S413 keeps #595 and mismatch denials plus wrapper/terminator controls;
  S414-S416 keep emitter ordering, compatibility, refusal and safe newline

  behavior; clarify that fences remain checked under option B and retain

  drift tests, parsing the hook's three-field output by tab. S419 keeps
  instructing-doc and grammar-owner pins, with
  OR31 and its existing stamp untouched.
- **S412 historical fixture addendum (#728, 2026-11-26):** [A] Supersede
  "historical comparisons only where available" above for round 6. Track an
  immutable byte-for-byte copy of `hooks/agent-dispatch.py` from
  `2d93c255f06c3f89afde70b2625c1926a09754a5` at
  `test/fixtures/role-stage-599-previous.py`; SHA-256 of the source bytes is
  `de151be376dacf6ac1dde3807bc85ae6537af5afabda98b8a8566394fbbc5e71`.
  Developer extracts it once from the available local object; runtime uses

  Other pinned historical verdicts retain equality; do not rewrite prompts

  Exact historical bytes cannot be reworded to satisfy the retired-name

  Preserve this row when #685 (epic #742) later widens the guard; the

- **QA handoff, new cases:** [A] Add the round-7 bullet, numbered, dollar
  prompt, blockquote, `Run:`, `cd ... &&` and `bash -c` introduction shapes
  with correct, missing-prefix and mismatching commands; apostrophes
  before/after/on non-emit prose lines must not change their verdicts.
  Include malformed bare prose mentions followed by a wrong command.
  Add independent emit units before/after malformed prose, mismatches in

  Pin consumed value text containing role/stage flags, comments containing

  Require the single unchecked diagnostic for malformed relevant units,

  Observe unsupported shell/tab cases and legacy stage-prefix/equals gaps

  implicit quote continuation, skipped mid-line mismatch, ignored size

- **Delivery, evidence and remaining decisions:** [V] This Planning review

- **Violated when:** [A] prose on an unrelated line changes a parsed emit
