### A49 — Preserve the oracle at a conflict and across the QA handoff (#547, #546; F59, F60; amends A4, A12, A28, A41, A42)

Settled choices below are temporary panel decisions (2026-10-30, Q2–Q6), subject to TiesL's overrule.

- **Why.** In #505 the Developer's red run exposed a false preserved-behavior clause, then the scenario was changed to fit the code. Disclosure was the only provenance evidence. Preserve the conflict evidence and QA's exact handoff without changing the scenario/file sync check or QA's scope.
- **AC-versus-design review.** #547 AC1–AC6 and #546 AC1–AC3, AC5–AC6: no contradiction or narrowing. #546 AC4 is narrowed: any owning-role-resolved scenario change after the Developer step requires a new QA artifact and a matching comparison before Review; explaining a nonzero comparison is insufficient. Prior differences and findings remain linked; Product's AC4 must be amended accordingly.
- **Stop and ownership (OR19, Developer A4, Shared).** A Developer or QA encountering a design defect or a spec/scenario conflict stops the affected change before altering the oracle. Preserve `PRD.md`, `ARCHITECTURE.md` and `TEST-SCENARIOS.md` byte-identically as they stood at detection, including earlier legitimate owner edits. Save the attempted patch under A12 before any revert; report the existing finding class, falsifying check and evidence, then follow OR17/A28. Wrong/ambiguous requirements are `spec`, faulty tests are `test`, structural decisions are `design`; unresolved classification uses OR18. Disclosure does not authorize an edit. Developer A4's docs permission explicitly excludes authored edits to all three files; committing owner-authored text with tests does not transfer authorship. Only under a valid `skip=Test` record (OR34) (skip=Test exemption: panel 2026-10-31, PR #605), the Developer may append new `### <ID>` entries and scenario text to `TEST-SCENARIOS.md` for test files it adds in this work item, leaving existing text byte-identical; OR19 and this stop still apply. The stop lasts until the owning-role route resolves the conflict.
- **Historical claims (write-spec, Product/QA, tdd-seams).** Replace write-spec's unconditional instruction to update specs when implementation diverges with owner-routed reconciliation. Each current/existing/unchanged-behavior clause records the observed `main` SHA, the PR's main merge-base SHA separately when different, a falsifying command/check, observable expected result and Product/QA's run evidence or concrete evidence lookup. Run the preservation assertion on the merge base and revalidate relevant main changes before merge. It must be green there; red is a `spec` finding and invokes the stop, not new-behavior TDD evidence. Unverified claims remain unresolved. New behavior still needs red-before-green. Architect's contract explicitly names every AC contradicted or narrowed, or states none.
- **Artifact Interface (QA report, before Implementation).** QA posts `git diff --full-index` of `TEST-SCENARIOS.md` against the base in a tilde fence in its report comment, with the full base SHA, `base_sha256` and `result_sha256`. Reconstruct outside the repository by applying the unified diff to `git show <base>:TEST-SCENARIOS.md`, verifying the base and reconstructed-result hashes. A mismatch fails closed. An unchanged file still needs an explicit artifact and equal hashes. The existing report Interface carries the evidence; no general patch Module is introduced.
- **Comment transport.** Read the raw comment body, not rendered text. QA verifies its published artifact before handoff. Base64 of the same unified diff is the transport fallback when hashes fail in transit; both hashes must still verify. Missing, truncated or unusable evidence leaves the handoff unresolved. A report over the comment limit leaves it unresolved and triggers the pushed-ref alternative; never silently truncate or substitute local files. Comments provide checked recoverability, not immutability.
- **Comparison contract (OR46(c)).** Inputs: repository identity, selected QA report comment ID, full Developer head SHA and applicable base SHA. Validate the artifact against its recorded base and both hashes; compare the whole committed `TEST-SCENARIOS.md` byte for byte with the reconstructed QA result. If the branch merged main after handoff, re-apply QA's unified diff to the new base and compare against that result. Failed reconstruction is unusable evidence. Exit 0 means match, 1 different, 2 unusable evidence; only 0 permits Review. Reconstruction stays outside the repository, with no repository writes. The exact command lives in the role-contract text. The comparison verifies bytes, not authorship or semantic correctness.
- **Handoff, logging and Review (OR15, QA/Reviewer contracts, pre-merge-review).** Each changed QA handoff gets a new linked report explicitly superseding and retaining earlier reports. Resume selects the applicable artifact from durable records; absent/unreadable evidence stops. After Developer returns, compare its committed head. Each differing hunk needs a disclosed finding and owning-role resolution; the orchestrator authors no reconciliation. Any owner-resolved scenario change returns to QA for a new artifact and matching comparison before Review. Record each attempt: `QA provenance: command=<exact invocation>; artifact=<comment URL>; base=<SHA>; base_sha256=<hash>; qa_sha256=<hash>; head=<SHA>; committed_sha256=<hash>; exit=<status>; result=match|different|unresolved; findings=<links or none>; supersedes=<artifact URL or none>`. Unknown identities use `unavailable`. OR15 retains its existing fields and adds the applicable QA artifact, comparison log and finding/resolution links. Reviewer verifies provenance and test fidelity; the scenario/file sync gate and QA's no-test-code scope stay unchanged. Only a valid `skip=Test` record (OR34, as read by the merge guard) (skip=Test exemption: panel 2026-10-31, PR #605) exempts the QA artifact, comparison and associated Reviewer approval block, with the orchestrator logging `QA provenance: result=not-applicable; skip=<record URL>; head=<SHA>` and the Reviewer verifying that record and log for the reviewed head instead; `single-session` alone does not exempt.
- **QA test strategy, through agreed Seams.** QA specifies scenarios; Developer writes/runs test code. Loaded skill/core text covers stop, A4 exclusions, historical evidence, Architect's consistency line and the preservation exception. The comparison Interface covers equal, one-byte difference, CRLF/whitespace, missing or truncated artifact, and superseded handoff. Use independent byte fixtures; assert no repository writes.
- **Existing pins and behavior evidence.** OR19 changes touch S214 (`s214_route_by_class.sh`, including its Shared-text assertions and OR19 inventory location), S311 (`s311_orchestrator_inventory_and_parts.sh`, inventory and OB coverage), and OB20. OR15 changes touch S210 (`s210_review_brief_from_artifacts.sh`), S311's `OR15 Review round brief` mutation anchor, and OB13; preserve its existing carry-forward fields. Update `skills/role-contracts/orchestrator-rules.tsv` coverage/name and add affected OB cases without renumbering IDs. OR15 and OR19 are judgment-tier, so their wording has no SHA pin in `test/fixtures/orchestrator-core-pins.tsv`; do not regenerate unrelated core pins to make checks pass. Keep S68's red-before-green anchor while adding the preservation exception. S318 must measure both injected slots against `CONTEXT_BUDGET_CHARS=9000`, retain 500 characters of headroom for slot 2 and the OR47/OR48 fallback consistency; if they move, update S311's part lists and inventory together. Put detailed artifact syntax/command in role-contracts rather than bloating the injected core. Text pins alone do not establish obedience: extend `test/behavior/orchestrator-scenarios.md` for spec-conflict stops, missing artifact, comparison/logging and unauthorized-diff routes; run `test/behavior/orchestrator-diff.sh --base <identified-main-SHA>` once for the final coordinated text and commit its fresh `test/behavior/orchestrator-diff.stamp`. The current runner has no scenario filter and its stamp covers the core plus the entire scenario file, so log that stamp requirement as OR48's reason for the full shared run, including coordinated #528 wording only if actually included. Any subsequent core/scenario change requires fresh matching evidence. No behavior run, S274 or full check is part of this Planning session.
- **Scope and cost.** Adoption/meaning-version decisions and #530 restructuring remain outside this amendment. Architect effort is small; Developer/QA estimate fixtures and the shared paid behavior run separately.


### A50 — Stage selection applies human class decisions; it creates no waiver authority (#647; F61, F62; amends A18 and A41)

Temporary, panel decision: panel 1, 2026-11-03, D3-D7; subject to maintainer acceptance under OR43. These entries design the settled issue, not a grant of either class waiver.

- **Threat model first.** [V] The header of `skills/pre-merge-review/model-record-gate.sh` explicitly cannot verify override authorship, agent identity or work-item attribution. Any session can forge records, including a human-looking `decided-by`; timestamps and links are evidence, not authentication. [A] Mitigation is the orchestrator's posting discipline, unchanged human authority, independent scrutiny and visible acceptance of temporary decisions. A panel name blacklist, another forgeable marker, or a merge-time panel check would not establish authority. There is no gate, parser, hook or `pipeline-override.sh` change in #647, including no rejection of a panel name by the script. A script accepting such a name is not permission for the orchestrator to use it.
- **One policy Module and its Interface.** [A] Put the normative stage-selection procedure in a subsection `Stage-selection panel` under `Running the pipeline` in `skills/role-contracts/SKILL.md`; keep the Abbreviated workflow and a `Standing human class decisions` subsection in that same section. The panel brief must explicitly reference/read these subsections, the issue's ACs, Discovery report, proposed file scope and the applicable human source; the issue/panel record alone is not the procedure. `policy/WORKFLOW.md` replaces its long Abbreviated bullet with a reference to that source, including a direct pointer to the panel subsection. This always-loaded policy reference supplies the entry point without growing the injected core. The canonical skill owns class conditions, authority, timing, record format, escalation and review-depth preservation. Its existing script invocation, single-quote instruction, `pipeline-override.sh --help` refusal pointer and `Closes #<issue>` requirement remain there. [V] OR34 already describes the generic human override and the Abbreviated scope. [A] Retain it byte-identically as a frozen compatibility synopsis, not a second editable definition of the new class-selection rules; pins check agreement with the canonical section. No new class defaults or panel exceptions go into OR34. This is an A41 placement amendment: these additional rules are reached through the always-loaded policy reference and the panel brief, rather than by extending the core. It does not claim that a reference proves live loading or obedience.
- **Managed projections.** [V] `lib/workflow-adapters.py` generates `WORKFLOW.md` from `policy/WORKFLOW.md` plus `adapters/claude/INSTRUCTIONS.md`, generates `adapters/codex/AGENTS.md` using `adapters/codex/INSTRUCTIONS.md`, and copies that payload into root `AGENTS.md`'s managed block. [A] Change policy source only for this rule; adapter INSTRUCTIONS files retain runtime mapping and references rather than acquiring their own class definitions. Regenerate with `./generate-workflow-adapters.sh`, verify with `./check-workflow-adapters.sh`; never hand-edit these outputs or an adopted project's generated `AGENTS.md`. `CLAUDE.md`, where installed as the `WORKFLOW.md` symlink, inherits the projection; it is absent in this clone and must not be created here. `README.md`'s script row and Product's descriptive PRD text point to the same source instead of becoming independent class catalogues. No generator code change is needed.
- **Core cost constraint.** [V] S318 measures injected output with the common context-budget constant and a separate slot-2 headroom floor; the dispatch reports only one character of remaining slot-2 headroom. [A] Preserve all bytes of `skills/role-contracts/ORCHESTRATOR.md`, its inventory, core pins, existing behavior scenarios and differential stamp. Do not pay for or claim a core differential run for #647. Any later proposal to change that core is a separate, budgeted change with A41's differential evidence, not a fixup hidden in this item.
- **Selection algorithm.** [A] After a separately marked Discovery and before any work-item commit or PR opening, Product, Architect and the orchestrator each take a position on the stages needed by the ACs and proposed diff. This consultation is not the Planning stage and never supplies its marker. They may consider only Planning, Test and Implementation, within an evidenced standing human class. A unanimous in-class selection may be applied by the orchestrator. A 2-1 vote to skip, any recommendation outside a class, unverifiable source/conditions, or a proposal to skip Review is referred to the maintainer with no panel-derived posting. A majority to retain work retains it; dissent is recorded. No majority can waive AC1. Missing participants or evidence leave selection unresolved; continue the full required pipeline or resolve the question before a skip. Do not silently remove a scope from the named Abbreviated pair: any differently scoped waiver requires applicable separate human authority.
- **Protected work, every variant.** [A] Preserve the orchestrator, fresh Reviewer Review, Discovery with its own model-record (issue text never substitutes), each AC-dependent stage, and at least one role other than the author seeing the change. An AC adding a scenario requires Test; a diff touching executable code requires Implementation, including executable tests and scripts. These checks precede class classification: a file named documentation or test-only is not enough. Abbreviated selection is unavailable if its Test skip would violate those conditions. Doc-only/test-only can skip Implementation only within verified human conditions and when neither the ACs nor executable diff requires it. `skip=X` outside an applicable class and `single-session` remain explicit per-item human override requests under OR34, not panel defaults. This mechanism never derives a single-session waiver, skipped Discovery or skipped Review from a vote. Existing generic script/gate grammar is unchanged, even where it can represent a broader human override. A request conflicting with protected work escalates; the panel cannot silently amend #647's AC1. A valid `skip=Test` retains A49's exemption and Developer append-only scenario scope; `single-session` alone still supplies no QA-provenance exemption.
- **Standing class catalogue and evidence status.** [V] Panel D3 names exactly two standing classes. The current canonical skill, policy, PRD F38 and OR34 verify the *documented* Abbreviated scope (`skip=Planning` plus `skip=Test`), human grant, upfront script posting, unchanged words, retained Discovery/Implementation/fresh Review and A49 exception. [A] They are model/policy statements, not the original human words granting reusable standing authority. `https://github.com/TiesL/spec-driven-guardrails/issues/564` is a provenance lead for the named track, not a verified quotation or verified comment link in this offline session. Record the actual human quotation or durable comment link before enabling class application; do not use this lead or a paraphrase as `reason`. [A] For test-only/doc-only `skip=Implementation`, D3 verifies the intended class name and scope, but no original human words, durable human comment or exact eligibility conditions were found in the searched repository texts. Do not invent a blanket documentation/test exception. Both catalogue rows must carry human identity, original words or a durable source with recoverable words, permitted scopes and exact conditions. Unverified rows remain visibly unresolved and cannot authorize a posting; obtain evidence or a new explicit per-item human waiver. D3's temporary panel record is not itself the human source. No third standing class is introduced.
- **Posting Interface and record.** [A] Post a separate ordinary issue comment, not a waiver marker, containing `temporary, panel decision`, a stable decision ID, the question, named Product/Architect/orchestrator positions, vote (including dissent), outcome with exact selected stages, and a link to the standing human words applied. For an out-of-class recommendation state that no standing words apply and link the per-item human decision before any posting. Include evidence of class eligibility and protected-work checks; link Discovery. After a permitted outcome, only the orchestrator runs `pipeline-override.sh` from the project checkout, with the human identity as `--decided-by`, exactly their unchanged words as the single-quoted `--reason`, and only the authorized scopes. Preserve the script's validation and round trip; unrepresentable words require new human words, never sanitizing or truncation. Save/link the posted waiver comment in the panel record or Pipeline log and verify the returned text. The issue must be linked from the PR by `Closes #<issue>` in title/body. A panel record alone never waives a missing stage. If #645 lands, adopt its shared record definition by an explicit follow-up, preserving this required information rather than assuming that dependency already exists.
- **Timeliness Interface.** [A] Both the completed panel decision and applicable script posting must precede *both* the first commit made for this work item and PR creation, not merely push, Review or merge. This includes a spec-only, test-only, empty or later-squashed work-item commit, in any session; inherited release/base commits are excluded. The orchestrator records the branch's initial base SHA and first work-item commit identity (or `none yet`), decision/waiver comment identities and creation times, and PR creation identity/time when available in the Pipeline log. Compare the earlier of first work-item commit and PR creation to the later required record creation. Unknown order or a tie is unresolved, not timely. Adding fields by editing a late comment cannot backdate completion; publish a superseding record with its actual time. Rebasing, squashing or deleting the first commit does not reset the deadline; retain the original identities in the log. These are posting-rule evidence, not a new timestamp merge gate. A late record remains visible as late and cannot establish advance selection; seek a specific human resolution rather than retroactively calling it compliant.
- **Review depth and acceptance.** [A] Selection changes stage presence only. Retain A13's required review depth or raise it with `--force-thorough`; never lower it through a waiver or a doc-only label. At merge-approval preparation list every relevant panel decision, its record link and outcome, including retained-work, escalated and superseded decisions with their resolution links. Flag each decision widening a limit or accepting risk for explicit acceptance, including these temporary spec decisions and the removal of #645 as a dependency. OR43 remains in force; neither a unanimous panel nor merge into a release branch constitutes maintainer acceptance of spec changes. Keep release-branch merge handling and main approval requirements as they stand.
- **AC consistency.** [A] No contradiction or narrowing of #647 AC1-AC7 is proposed. AC4's single source is the canonical Running section; unchanged OR34 remains its existing compatible generic synopsis, not a new independent class definition. Evidence gaps are not new eligibility defaults. If the canonical human source proves a class incompatible with AC1, stop that application and route the conflict to Product/the maintainer; do not relax either rule. All rules above have been checked against Abbreviated, single-session, individual `skip=X`, doc-only and test-only variants.

### A51 — Verify posting discipline through existing Seams; reserve S534-S548 (#647; F61-F63)

- **Decomposition.** [A] Keep one policy Module in the canonical Running section and the existing posting Module `pipeline-override.sh`. The Interface is the eligibility/decision/posting procedure and the script's existing issue/scopes/human/words arguments. The Seams are source text read as data, the script CLI with `--dry-run` or `PIPELINE_OVERRIDE_GH` capture, and an instruction-following exercise given the canonical section plus panel brief. Real GitHub and the existing local command stub are actual Adapters; no new production dispatcher, panel parser, authority detector or general decision framework is justified. Deletion test: removing the canonical rules would spread their complexity into policy, briefs and tests, so centralizing provides Depth, Leverage and Locality. A wrapper that merely encodes expected decisions would add no Depth and must not become a substitute for testing the orchestrator.
- **Mechanical versus judgment evidence.** [A] Offline tests can pin the loaded source's protections, canonical links and catalogue evidence fields; check generated projection equality; snapshot unchanged core/script/gate bytes; and exercise the existing CLI to check exact scope/human/reason/comment issue and round-trip output. They cannot authenticate the human, establish that a class really applies, prove the orchestrator read a linked rule, or prove refusal to post from a hand-written expected command. QA must specify instruction-following pipeline-override-use exercises for those judgments: supply the actual Running section and panel brief, AC/diff/class evidence and event ordering; observe whether the orchestrator calls the posting command, escalates or retains stages. Capture attempted commands with the existing `PIPELINE_OVERRIDE_GH` test Adapter and inspect issue/body/arguments; prohibited cases require no attempted posting, not a script error. Never grade those cases by passing a `panel` string to a merge gate. No production or merge-gate change is permitted by D7.
- **Test-ID plan (QA owns final scenario text).** [A] Allocate S534-S548, all used below; each has a matching `test/cases/s<ID>_stage_selection.sh` entry and appropriate F61/F62/F63 Covers links. S534: canonical source and managed references (AC4). S535: required minimal record and human-source link, missing-field controls (AC2). S536: separately marked Discovery before consultation, never replaced by issue text (AC1). S537: preserve orchestrator, fresh Review and independent scrutiny (AC1/AC3). S538: AC-dependent Test and executable-diff Implementation, including executable tests (AC1). S539: unanimous eligible Abbreviated pair, unchanged human words and A49 handling, plus scenario-adding AC refusal (AC1/AC2/AC4). S540: eligible doc-only skip=Implementation and ineligible executable/configuration counterexamples (AC1/AC2/AC4). S541: test-only class with verified conditions versus executable test diff requiring Implementation (AC1/AC2/AC4). S542: a 2-1 skip vote escalates, unanimous retain and dissent recording controls (AC3). S543: unsupported class/skip=X and single-session require explicit per-item human authority, panel record alone insufficient (AC2/AC3). S544: human decided-by, byte-exact reason, script refusal without rewriting, and closing-issue linkage (AC2). S545: first-commit/PR ordering, equality/unknown/late edit, inherited-base and rebase controls (AC5). S546: merge request lists every relevant decision/link/outcome and flags risk/limit decisions (AC6). S547: A13 depth retained or raised with --force-thorough, never reduced (AC7). S548: unchanged production gate/script/core, no panel-name authentication claim, and unresolved original human evidence blocks class posting (AC2/AC4; threat limit). Test class positives use explicitly labelled synthetic human evidence fixtures, never pretend that those fixtures settle the real catalogue gaps.
- **Mutation controls and exercise evidence.** [A] Every new mechanical assertion first passes on an unmutated sandbox copy, then fails for its own diagnostic after one targeted deletion/change: remove a protection, human-source field, reference, timeliness clause, escalation rule, risk flag or depth restriction. Check mutations actually apply; a red check caused by missing unrelated data is not detection. Retain byte-exact reason controls and issue-number mismatch probes through the CLI. Instruction exercises pair permitted/refused cases differing in one eligibility fact or event order; record supplied text identity, inputs, observed action and captured posting or absence. Include a deliberately permissive instruction mutant to demonstrate the judgment exercise can expose an unauthorized call. Static pins remain static evidence even if all green. Developer executes these exercises through the available runtime in isolation and reports the transcript/results; absent runtime or human-source evidence stays unresolved, not a fabricated pass. No change to the existing core behavior runner/scenario file/stamp is required: that runner loads ORCHESTRATOR, not this new canonical section, and would not test this Interface. QA defines these dedicated exercises in `test/behavior/stage-selection-scenarios.md`; results go in the Developer report, not a new core stamp. Automated case files check the corresponding mechanical subset only and must label that limit.
- **Existing tests requiring coordinated owner changes.** [V] S378 currently requires the Abbreviated scopes independently in policy and skill. [A] Change it to require the canonical policy reference plus the full normative definition only in the skill, with mutation arms for either reference or source loss; preserve its unchanged OR34, session-context script mention, single-quote, help and closing-keyword checks. QA updates the S378 scenario text explicitly. `test/fixtures/codex-455.py` currently pins `Abbreviated workflow` and `pipeline-override.sh` in the root managed block: retain these as reference labels in the short policy pointer, so S294 and its mutation anchors remain valid without editing that fixture. Keep the `- **Abbreviated workflow**` bullet shape for its deletion control. S318's code, thresholds and inventory stay unchanged; run it after generation as regression evidence of no core-budget growth, never loosen it to make this item pass. Existing S376/S377 script tests remain valid.
- **Product handoff, no Architect PRD edit.** [A] Product adds F61 (selection and protected work, AC1/AC3), F62 (human class authority, canonical source, record and upfront posting, AC2/AC4/AC5), and F63 (decision disclosure and depth, AC6/AC7). They must distinguish script validation from orchestrator authorization, retain forgeability limits, mark unresolved original words/eligibility, explain single-session is not a panel class and preserve A49. Product updates F38's descriptive Abbreviated paragraph to point to Running rather than independently define class defaults. The separate Discovery marker and AC-dependent Test/executable Implementation rules must be explicit; no invented documentation/test waiver conditions. These are owner-authored spec changes requiring OR43 visibility, not Developer doc edits.
- **Exact file handoff.** [A] Architect: append A50/A51 in `ARCHITECTURE.md` only. Product: `PRD.md` F61-F63 and the F38 reference. QA: `TEST-SCENARIOS.md` S534-S548 and S378, plus scenario strategy for `test/behavior/stage-selection-scenarios.md` (Developer materializes that executable-exercise input from QA's strategy). Developer: `skills/role-contracts/SKILL.md`, `policy/WORKFLOW.md`, `test/cases/s378_pipeline_override_doc_text_pins.sh`, the fifteen `test/cases/s534_stage_selection.sh` through `test/cases/s548_stage_selection.sh`, shared private test fixture `test/fixtures/stage-selection-647.py`, and `test/behavior/stage-selection-scenarios.md`; generate `WORKFLOW.md`, `adapters/codex/AGENTS.md` and root `AGENTS.md`. Developer also updates the README script-row reference, `CHANGES.md` and `CHANGELOG.md`. Runtime INSTRUCTIONS, generator/checker code, Codex fixture, S318, pipeline script, gate, core and core behavior evidence need no changes. Any newly discovered required production edit is a design finding, not authorization to expand this list silently.
- **Adoption and changelog.** [A] Add one #647 entry to `CHANGELOG.md` Unreleased describing standing human authority, upfront selection records, escalation, disclosure and unchanged gate limitations. `CHANGES.md` needs one #647 notice by extending `process-multi-agent-roles` Yes means with a canonical-source reference and the new selection/record obligation, not a second rule catalogue. Recommend meaning v3 (current row is v2); material obligations change, so this is a maintainer decision under OR43 and must be accepted before Developer applies the bump. Retain its established PR provenance and link the delivering #647 PR for the amendment once known. Add `always-loaded: WORKFLOW.md` to Reaches session for the policy entry point; keep existing delivery fields, do not claim the whole skill is automatically injected. No new opt-in or separate class-waiver authority is designed. #651's later notice stays separate, per D2.
- **Validation and effort.** [A] Planning checks adapter drift, English-only policy and traceability, plus append-only diff integrity; it runs no live panel, network, paid behavior test or git mutation. Developer runs new/affected cases, S378, S318, S294, existing override cases, generator drift and required static checks after coordinating Product/QA text. Reviewer judges authority/class evidence and actual instruction exercise results, not just green pins. Planning effort is small; QA/Developer effort is moderate because decision behavior requires separate evidence from text pins. Original human words/conditions and temporary panel acceptance remain maintainer-visible open items; this design never claims they were verified offline.

### A52 — Epic release PRs derive stage coverage from their children (#651; F64–F66)

[A] Planning design, 2026-11-03, for the settled #651 AC1–AC14 and panel-1
D1–D9; temporary panel choices remain subject to maintainer acceptance (OR43).
#647 lands first; A50–A51 belong to that work item. This entry reserves no
other IDs and does not implement the gate or amend Product's requirements.
Amended in place after Review round 1 on PR #658 (findings
real-scale-timeout-unchecked, closing-404-forces-legacy,
epic-output-unattributed-noise, s548-gate-hash-pin-red,
child-override-source-untested): discovery no longer scans every repository
issue, reads run in a bounded pool, and output is attributed.
[V] Measured 2026-11-03 on TiesL/spec-driven-guardrails: one `gh api` detail
read 0.48–0.53 s, a 100-object page 0.97 s; 40 detail reads took 19.6 s
serially, 4.8 s with 4 and 2.8 s with 8 concurrent reads. The repository has
658 issue/PR objects (7 pages, 389 issues). One private gate subprocess
(`--epic-live`/`--epic-closing`) costs about 0.155 s, so the old per-issue scan
spent about 60 s in subprocesses alone. The old worker made about 210 gh
calls plus about 430 shell subprocesses for the 19-child shape (above 120 s
serially); the design below needs about 213 gh calls, 8 at a time, and a
constant number of shell subprocesses per phase.

- **Module, Interface and Locality.** Keep `model-record-gate.sh <pr-number>`
  as the one public Interface: findings on stdout, exit 0, only `role-played: `
  blocks. Its Module owns inheritance and stage decisions. Add one private
  helper, `lib/model-record-epic.py`, for bounded REST traversal, JSON decoding,
  cached data and set comparisons. Invoke with `python3 -I`, argument arrays,
  no shell evaluation. It returns a versioned JSON manifest in a temporary
  directory, never marker syntax or final gate findings. The gate applies
  `live_text`, `rec_scan_bundle` and `rec_field` from the existing shell libs;
  no Python copy of Markdown or record grammar. Missing Python/helper or a
  malformed manifest is unchecked in the inheritance path. Bash remains 3.2:
  indexed arrays, no associative arrays, mapfile or lowercase expansions.
  The private shell modes `--epic-live` and `--epic-closing` take many bodies
  per call, framed by the record separator byte (removed from bodies first),
  and return one framed result per body in order; a count mismatch is
  unchecked. The helper therefore spawns a constant number of shell
  subprocesses per phase instead of one per body. The helper runs gh reads
  and `--epic-evaluate` context scans in one bounded pool of 8 concurrent
  subprocesses (`concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor`, stdlib); each keeps
  its own process group. Only the main thread installs signal handlers; it
  tracks live process groups under a lock and kills them all on SIGTERM,
  deadline or the first failure, cancelling queued work. Counters and caches
  are lock-protected. Results are merged in sorted context/child/PR order,
  never completion order, so output is deterministic. The gate's worker only
  formats the ordered results.
  The deletion test puts transport/set complexity back into the gate; the
  helper earns Depth by hiding traversal behind one manifest, rather than
  exposing one wrapper per endpoint. Leverage and Locality stay in this Module.
  The real `gh` and the fixture `gh` are the two Adapters at the existing PATH
  Seam. No new configuration port or changes to the shared record reader.
- **[A] Recognition and compatibility (#663 F2/F3).** The shell first calls

### A53 — A18 override semantics retain compatibility for epic inheritance (#651)

[A] This decision amends A18's override paragraph by reference; retain its
historical text in place. Grammar and human-only OR34 authority do not change.
A valid manual override on the epic keeps the entire legacy gate path and its
byte-identical output (A52); this includes partial skips and single-session.
Otherwise inheritance adds evidence reads, not a new waiver type. A valid skip
already visible in the release PR's legacy evidence pool, including a skip on
ANY issue named by a closing keyword, waives that stage's absence for the whole
release PR. For an inherited stage it also removes the per-child missing-stage
obligation at that release gate; it does not grant a waiver on the child issue
or change the child's own gate. Membership reconciliation still runs in the
inheritance path. A skip does not waive multi-stage-text findings. Review is
not inherited; a release-wide skip=Review or single-session retains its legacy
waiver effect, although standing panel policy cannot authorize skipping Review.
Child-local evidence fetched only for inheritance never joins the release-wide
override pool. A child single-session alone supplies no inherited missing stage.

[V] F66 requires the release Closes set to include epic #655 and its children;
#663 AC1 extends the concrete set to #647, #651, #660 and #663. [A] Keep
that set explicit in release body, Pipeline log and approval request, with
every release-wide skip effect (AC13). Excluding self from child closers changes
neither overrides nor panel authority; no panel contract change is needed.
The release-membership meaning-version decision remains with maintainer.
[A] Maintainer acceptance under OR43 must name the A18 amendment and the
release-membership amendment, alongside all temporary panel decisions and the
panel-2 QA scope departure. No new override author, marker or orchestrator-core
rule is introduced.

### A55 — The epic auto-close decision asks two release-signal queries, only at the moment it would close (#683; partial of #671)

- **Placement (Locality).** [A] `epic-auto-close.sh` already ends in one decision
  (`NONE` / `STILL_OPEN` / `CLOSE`). The release-signal check runs only inside the
  `CLOSE` arm, immediately before `gh issue close`, as a small function in the same
  script. An epic with open children, no children, or already closed never pays for
  the two queries (the common case on every issue close). No new module or seam: the
  existing `gh` call seam, which the fake-`gh` tests already use, is the only seam.
- **Query form (exactness once, client-side).** [V, run against this repo with
  `gh` 2.102.0] Branches: `gh api --paginate "repos/{owner}/{repo}/git/matching-refs/heads/release/N-"
  --jq '"page", (.[].ref)'`; an open-PR list: `gh api --paginate
  "repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls?state=open&base=main&per_page=100" --jq '"page", (.[] |
  [.state, .base.ref, .head.ref, (.head.repo.full_name // ""), (.base.repo.full_name // "")] | @tsv)'`
  (as shipped in `release_signal`; an `awk` match keeps open, base `main`, head
  `release/N-*`, head repository equal to base repository).
  `--paginate` closes AC6 without a magic limit. The `"page"` line the jq emits once
  per page is the response sentinel: a legitimate empty result is one `page` line
  (matching-refs answers `[]`), so no output at all means the call failed or was
  malformed. [A] The script then keeps only lines matching `refs/heads/release/N-`
  or `release/N-` (N from the already-validated digit string) so exactness does not
  depend on server prefix semantics, and the fake `gh` can be tested with an
  over-broad response (AC4). The pulls endpoint has no prefix filter on head (`head=`
  needs an exact `owner:branch`), hence list-and-filter. A PR from a fork carrying a
  `release/N-` head name does not count: same-repository heads only, per the [maintainer decision, Pipeline log comment](https://github.com/TiesL/spec-driven-guardrails/issues/683#issuecomment-6725817396)
  (this replaces the first draft, which kept the epic open for a fork PR).
  Search (`gh pr list --search`) is rejected: index lag, which the script header
  already avoids for issues.
- **Order and short-circuit.** [A] Branch query first; if it finds a match the epic
  stays open without the PR query (exit 0, one stderr line naming the epic and the
  branch). A failed branch query exits non-zero at once. This narrows AC7 for the case
  where the branch is found and the PR query would have failed; resolved, see AC
  differences.
- **Token.** [V] `.github/workflows/ci.yml` records repo evidence (#83) that a job
  with an explicit `permissions:` block lacking `pull-requests: read` failed on a PR
  endpoint. [A, not fetched this session] GitHub's REST reference lists "Pull
  requests: read" for list-pull-requests and "Contents: read" for git refs
  (matching-refs). Decision: add `pull-requests: read` to `epic-auto-close.yml`
  (permissions then `contents: read`, `issues: write`, `pull-requests: read`). The
  repo is public, where reads may succeed unauthenticated; that is not relied on.
  A 403/404 is a failed query (AC7), not "no PR". [V] A nonexistent repo gives
  `gh api` exit 1 under `--paginate`.
- **Failure handling.** [A] Each query: non-zero exit, no output, or no `page`
  sentinel is a failure: stderr `epic-auto-close: epic #N: <branch|open-PR> query
  failed ...`, exit 1, epic left open. The existing "no fail-open" header rule holds.
- **Rule (d) (#683 item 4).** [A] Recommend dropping it from this work item. It
  changes `templates/check-pr-issue-link.sh`, which `adopt.sh` offers to adopters
  (the issue's own scaffolding out-of-scope line), needs an N-specific closing
  match the script does not have (today it only asks "references no issue"), and the
  `edited` trigger reruns the whole `check` job on every PR edit. The harm it
  prevents is visible and recoverable (an epic stays open until closed by hand); the
  harm of item 1 is the irreversible-looking premature close. Defer to the rest of
  #671.

- **AC differences (resolved by the maintainer; this entry no longer awaits a
  decision).** Per the [maintainer decision, Pipeline log comment](https://github.com/TiesL/spec-driven-guardrails/issues/683#issuecomment-6725817396) and the amended #683 body: AC7 is read as "only
  when no earlier signal already keeps the epic open", so a found branch skips the
  PR query and exits 0. AC11 and Item 4 are dropped (the Rule (d) bullet above is
  the reasoning, now historical). AC5 and rule (b) gain the same-repository-head
  condition (fork PRs do not count). AC7 "empty output": `page` only is a valid
  "none", no output at all is the failure. AC8/AC9: the fake `gh` carries a default

- **Effect of this update.** Documentation only, no scenario or code change:

### A54 addendum (2026-11-08) — The reserved contract-text class also covers `CHANGES.md`, `templates/` and `USER-CLAUDE.md` (#681; amends A54 D2, D6 and the S590 matrix row)

Append-only note. The A54 entry above is not edited; where it lists the class, read it

### A54 addendum (2026-11-09) — Holding-pen decisions for items 2-6 of #678 (amends A54 D6, the S589/S590/S591/S593 matrix rows and the F68 wording; no contract text changes)

Append-only note. The A54 entry and the 2026-11-08 addendum above are not edited; where
they differ from this note on the points below, this note prevails. Planning for #678
(release branch `release/607-panel-mechanisms`, tip `0672da0`). Item 1 (null list
fields) needs no design decision beyond the diagnostics fixed at the end.

- **Item 2: S591 prior-result domain.** [A] `experiments[].prior[].result` takes the
  domain `denied`, `none` (the S590 `prior_denials` domain). A prior row is malformed
  when its `id` is not `present` (existing rule) OR its `result` is outside that domain
  (`UNKNOWN`, empty, null, or key missing). A malformed row on ANY prior row, matching
  or not, gives `591/experiment/denied-retry` and makes the experiment `denied` (the
  existing `malformed_prior` path: disposition `refused`, `attempts == []`, otherwise
  `denied-retry` again), so a matching identity with a bad result is read as denied,
  never as `none`. Chosen over validating only matching rows because the oracle already
  fails closed on a malformed `id` in any row; one `malformed_prior` rule, not two.
  Matrix row S591 gains "prior result `denied`/`none`".
- **Item 3: dissent on `unresolved`/`escalated`.** [A] Not allowed. The expected
  `dissent` is the computed minority for a `resolved` 2-1, `[]` otherwise, so any
  `unresolved` or `escalated` record whose `dissent` is not exactly `[]` (including
  null) gives `589/<id>/dissent`. The key stays required (present, may be empty), so
  a missing `dissent` is still `589/<id>/dissent`. Rationale: dissent is a vote artifact
  and `positions` already records each member's stance; this parallels
  `/fabricated-vote`. The skill says dissent is "recorded" with a vote; it nowhere
  allows it without one, so no SKILL.md change. Matrix row S589 gains "unresolved/
  escalated has no vote and no dissent".
- **Item 4: tokens that carry a target.** [A] `TARGETED` becomes six tokens: the
  existing `docs-pr`, `temporary-spec-choice`, `policy-choice` plus `readme-pr`,
  `changelog-unreleased-pr`, `meaning-version-bump` (each edits a repository file, so
  a contract-text file can be the target). Excluded, with reason: `close-issue`,
  `comment-issue`, `comment-pr`, `label-issue`, `label-pr`, `delete-merged-branch`
  have no file target (a comment is not an edit; rule text proposed in a comment still
  needs its own file-editing proposal, which is targeted); `merge-work-item-to-release`
  ignores target by T10. Behaviour for a targeted token is unchanged from the three
  already covered: target `panel-rules` becomes `edit-panel-rules` and is referred;
  `UNKNOWN`/empty/missing gives `590/<token>/target`; `other` stays eligible. For the
  seven untargeted eligible tokens the `target` field is not read (no diagnostic for
  any value). The reserved-class sentence in the skill is token-agnostic ("any
  proposal whose target is contract text ... eligible docs edit or policy choice"),
  so no SKILL.md change is needed; the S590 matrix row's "otherwise eligible
  `docs-pr` or `temporary-spec-choice`/`policy-choice` proposal" reads as "the six
  targeted tokens" from here.
- **Item 5: S593 protection rows tied (explicit amendment of D6).** [A] D6 says to
  protect the nine conditions "independently of a `retained` disposition or any
  supplied `eligible` list": independent of those two, never stated as independent of
  each other. This addendum nonetheless amends D6 explicitly: the four fact fields
  `adds_scenario`, `executable_diff`, `doc_only`, `requires` (the latter compared as a
  set; `selected` is a stage choice, not a fact, and is excluded) in the
  `unanimous-skip` row's embedded `protected` object must equal those of the
  `protected-work` row's `conditions` in the same record. Violation (including a
  missing or malformed field on either side, when both rows are present exactly
  once) gives `593/protection/unanimous-skip` (appended once). The other seven
  protections stay independent. Chosen over a single source (drop the embedded copy)
  because that changes the record shape and every `protected` fixture. Direction of the
  base-control fix: row 1 (`protected-work`) takes row 0's doc-only facts
  (`adds_scenario=False`, `executable_diff=False`, `doc_only=True`,
  `requires=['Discovery','Review']`, `selected` all stages), because row 0 is pinned to
  the grant's `actual` (doc-only) by the existing `executable_diff`/`doc_only` equality
  and by `grant_supports`; the reverse would make the skip grant lie.
- **Item 6: F68 wording.** [A] PRD.md F68, "the root PRD, ARCHITECTURE, TEST-SCENARIOS,
  which are not `templates/PRD.md` and its siblings" becomes "the root PRD, the rest of
  ARCHITECTURE (every entry except A54 D2), TEST-SCENARIOS, which are not
  `templates/PRD.md` and its siblings". PRD.md is Product-owned: Product (or the
  orchestrator) applies this exact wording; the Developer does not. No other text states
  the list ("root PRD" occurs only in F68).
- **Fixture plan.** [A] All in `test/fixtures/temporary-panel-645.py`; QA writes
  cases first, Developer the oracle. Oracle: (2) `malformed_prior` also tests
  `result not in ('denied','none')`; (3) compute `expected_dissent` outside the
  `resolved` branch; (4) `TARGETED` to six; (5) tie check after the protections loop in
  `authority_oracle`; (1) a list-or-malformed helper. Cases: S591 result matrix
  (4 bad values x matching and non-matching row, plus `none` control); S589 dissent on
  `unresolved` and `escalated` (non-empty, null, missing; `[]` control); every
  `TARGETED` loop (T1-T9, T6b widened labels) covers the three new tokens by the
  constant alone, plus one fixture per untargeted token that target `panel-rules`/
  `UNKNOWN` is ignored; S593 tie mutants per fact field and `requires` set. Existing
  fixtures that change a single protection row and are now expected to be red or must
  be mirrored on both rows: `protection_conditions()` row 1; the protected-work
  field True/False loop (~1031-1036); the `requires`/`selected` stage-list block
  (~1037-1056); `skip_case` (mirror its `protected` update onto row 1); the sweep at
  ~1290. Every control passing at `0672da0` must still pass (AC7); a control whose
  expectation flips because of the tie is mirrored, not loosened.
- **Item 1 diagnostics.** [A] `supersedes: None` gives `589/<id>/supersession`;
  `prior_denials: None` gives `590/<action>/denied-retry`; `result.attempts: None` gives
  `590/<action>/attempt`; `briefs[].payload: None` gives `591/<recipient>/brief`;
  `experiments[].prior: None` gives `591/experiment/denied-retry`. A missing key stays
  equal to an empty list.
- **Contract text.** [A] None of items 2-6 changes `skills/`, `ORCHESTRATOR.md` or
  A54 D2; nothing here is a maintainer-reserved edit. The F68 wording (item 6) is
  Product-owned spec text.
- **Doubts, recorded.** [A] (a) Item 4 excludes `comment-issue`: a comment can carry
  rule text, but is not an edit, so the proposal that edits is targeted instead; revisit
  if a panel ever executes a comment as the rule change. (b) Item 5 changes the base
  control's meaning of `protected-work` row 1 to doc-only, which weakens the
  executable-work coverage of the loops at ~1031-1056 unless QA keeps explicit
  executable variants (C2-C5 style) mirrored on both rows.

#### A57 addendum (Architect, Planning, 2026-11-09): S548 byte pins join the file list

Loop-back from QA (d63eddd, d0a7433) and the Developer. A57's file list missed
`test/fixtures/stage-selection-647.py`: its `SNAPSHOTS` pin the SHA-256 of
`ORCHESTRATOR.md`, `orchestrator-scenarios.md`, `orchestrator-core-pins.tsv` and
`orchestrator-diff.stamp` (S548), and the bundled edit must change the first three.

- **File list.** Add `test/fixtures/stage-selection-647.py` (the `SNAPSHOTS` entries
  only) to QA's files, with `TEST-SCENARIOS.md` S548 carrying an "Amended by #652"
  line. The waiver-authority and mutation controls are untouched.
- **Mechanism, checked.** QA's two-step is right. The stamp hashes only
  `ORCHESTRATOR.md` and the scenarios (`orchestrator_diff.py` `stamp_hash`), never the
  fixture, so re-pinning the fixture cannot make the stamp stale: no circularity.
  Dropping the stamp pin would be simpler but weakens a #647 oracle, which the
  maintainer decides, not this design; so the pin stays.
- **Order and owners.**
  1. Developer finishes the bytes of `ORCHESTRATOR.md`, the scenarios file and the
     pins file (A57 edits). Any later change to those bytes voids step 2.
  2. QA (Test) re-pins the three entries from the final bytes. The current pins are
     provisional, taken from the Developer's patch.
  3. The orchestrator runs the behavior run and commits the generated stamp (OR46 b);
     nobody hand-edits it or the fixture.
  4. QA, in a follow-up Test dispatch, re-pins only the `orchestrator-diff.stamp`
     entry, runs S548, S323 and S335, and pushes. This changes no stamped byte, so
     the stamp stays valid. Until step 4, S548 is red on the stamp pin by design.
  5. Merge only after step 4 is green; the stamp-pin dispatch is part of A57's done.
- **Violated when** (added to A57): an S548 pin of the three content files differs
  from the committed bytes at merge; the stamp pin differs from the committed stamp
  at merge; a pin is taken before the Developer's bytes are final; or the fixture is
  hand-edited by the orchestrator rather than re-pinned by QA.
- **Doubt, recorded.** [A] Dropping the stamp pin (stamp-check already covers
  staleness) would save one dispatch; kept because removing a pin is the
  maintainer's call.

#### A57 addendum 2 (Architect, Planning, 2026-11-09): S593 no longer byte-freezes `ORCHESTRATOR.md`

Loop-back from Review round 1 on PR #692 (finding `s593-orchestrator-byte-freeze`,
design/high; finding `or46c-comparison-pointer-cut`, design/low). S593's
`preservation_checks()` (`test/fixtures/temporary-panel-645.py`) requires
`skills/role-contracts/ORCHESTRATOR.md` to be byte-identical to `b22b476`. That was a
#645 scope guard ("remains byte-identical ... in this work"); #645 is merged, and #652
legitimately changes the file.

- **Decision.** Retire S593's byte pin for `ORCHESTRATOR.md` only, and replace it with a
  cross-reference check; do not re-point it. Reasons: (1) re-pointing makes a second
  copy of the pin S548 already holds (`SNAPSHOTS` in `stage-selection-647.py`), so every
  authorised core edit would need two re-pins and QA's two-step twice, which is the
  loop-back shape already seen once; (2) the guard's intent (no unreviewed drift of the
  core) is carried after #645 by S548's byte pin, `stamp-check` (core or scenario bytes
  change, behavior run required, OR46 b), and `orchestrator-core-pins.tsv` fragment pins;
  (3) narrowing to "the parts S593 really guards" has no content to narrow to: S593's
  only core claim was "untouched by #645", which is a statement about a finished diff.
- **What stays frozen.** The other `paths` in `preservation_checks()`
  (`pipeline-override.sh`, `orchestrator-rules.tsv`, `hooks/`, `skills/pre-merge-review/`)
  keep the `b22b476` byte pin, the ancestor check and the protected-byte mutation
  control; #652 touches none of them (`git diff --stat origin/main` confirms). The
  generated-projection checks are untouched.
- **Replacement check.** `preservation_checks()` asserts that `SNAPSHOTS` in
  `test/fixtures/stage-selection-647.py` has a pin for
  `skills/role-contracts/ORCHESTRATOR.md` (a text oracle, with a mutation control that
  rejects the fixture text with that entry removed). So dropping the S593 byte pin cannot
  silently leave the core unpinned; S548 does the byte comparison.
- **Other freezers, checked.** Grep of the test tree for `b22b476` finds only this
  fixture. SHA-256 literals appear in `stage-selection-647.py` (S548, handled by addendum
  1), `orchestrator-diff.stamp` (stamp), `orchestrator-core-pins.tsv` (fragment pins,
  re-pinned in A57), and unrelated hashes in `s159`, `s248` (a forbidden-name hash) and
  `completion-evidence.py` (the original stop-text hash). S316/S323/S335 hash through the
  stamp. Nothing else freezes `ORCHESTRATOR.md` bytes, so no third oracle loop-back is
  expected. The 593 clause `'ORCHESTRATOR.md remains byte-identical ... in this work.'`
  (`CLAUSES[593]`) is a pin of the panel's canonical wording, not a byte comparison, and
  stays: it is scoped to #645 by its own words. Do not edit it.
- **No `ORCHESTRATOR.md` byte changes.** Neither this resolution nor the finding 2
  decision below touches `ORCHESTRATOR.md`, the scenarios file or the pins file, so
  the stamp (OR46 b) stays valid and no behavior run is repeated. `stamp-check` must
  still say `stamp matches`.
- **File list.** QA (scenario text): `TEST-SCENARIOS.md` S593 gains an "Amended by #652
  (A57 addendum 2)" line: the `ORCHESTRATOR.md` byte snapshot moves to S548, S593 checks
  that the pin exists, the other snapshots remain; falsifier: the ORCHESTRATOR.md pin
  absent from `SNAPSHOTS` passes S593. Developer (test code):
  `test/fixtures/temporary-panel-645.py` `preservation_checks()` only (drop the path from
  `paths`, add the cross-reference check and its mutation control). Per the current
  contract QA writes scenarios and the Developer writes test code (open #684 covers the
  inconsistency in earlier loops). Order: the two edits are independent of the core
  bytes; run `bash test/cases/s593_temporary_panel.sh`, S548, S323, S335, then `./check`
  (CI on the head, both legs).
- **Finding 2 (`or46c-comparison-pointer-cut`): resolved without a byte change.** The
  pointer "(SKILL.md command/log)" was dropped deliberately. A fresh orchestrator holds the
  `role-contracts` skill (OR46 already assumes it: OR40 and OR21 point into `SKILL.md`
  the same way), whose "QA scenario comparison" section defines the command and the exact
  log line; the core keeps the obligation. Restoring about 25 characters would fit the
  headroom (576 / 606) but changes core bytes, re-staling the stamp and the behavior run,
  for a low whose damage is bounded by the Reviewer's own comparison. Deferred per OR40
  (a design low, not trivial); the A57 Q1 claim "each removed fragment is explanation or

- **D3 — The one configuration (AC3, D2).** [A] `policy/merge-autonomy.json`, read

  | Key | Type / shipped value | Meaning |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | `schema` | integer `1` | Format version. |
  | `repository` | `"TiesL/spec-driven-guardrails"` | Must equal the PR's repository. |
  | `enabled` | boolean, ships `false` | `true` is valid only with `acceptance` set (Q1, AC8). |

  | `executor_host` | string, `""` | `hostname -s` of the one machine that may execute; empty means no executor, so nothing executes. Set by the maintainer's config PR. |
  | `max_lines`, `max_files` | integers `300`, `8` | Inclusive; both counts must be 1..cap. Values below 1 are invalid. |
  | `hold_seconds` | integer `300` | At least 1; `0` is invalid. |
  | `groups.ordinary` | path patterns | `README.md`, `CONTEXT.md`, `PRD*.md` (root), `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `TEST-SCENARIOS.md`, `docs/**.md`, `prep/**.md`, `test/**`. |
  | `groups.adoption` | path patterns | A55's adoption list verbatim. |
  | `groups.guard` | path patterns | A55's guard/source list verbatim, minus `hooks/git-guardrails` (now reserved). |
  | `groups.generated` | `{ "outputs": [...], "inputs": [...] }` | Outputs `WORKFLOW.md`, `adapters/codex/AGENTS.md`, root `AGENTS.md` (managed block only); inputs `policy/WORKFLOW.md`, `adapters/*/INSTRUCTIONS.md`. |
  | `reserved.release` | path patterns | `CHANGELOG.md`, `VERSION`, `package.json`, `skills/release-branch-workflow/**`. |
  | `reserved.autonomy` | path patterns | `merge-preflight.sh`, `hooks/git-guardrails`, `skills/pre-merge-review/**`, `lib/model-record*`, `pipeline-override.sh`, `skills/role-contracts/**`, `skills/merge-risk-panel/**`, `policy/merge-autonomy.json`, `merge-risk-evidence.sh`, `lib/merge-risk*`, `test/cases/*merge_risk*`, `test/fixtures/merge-risk*`, `test/behavior/merge-risk*`. |
  | `labels.hold` | `["hold", "risk:*"]` | Present on PR or work-item issue: `held`. |
  | `labels.off` | `"merge-autonomy:off"` | On the control issue: global stop; on PR or issue: that item is referred. |
  | `release_heads` | `["release/*"]` | Matching head branch: referred. |

  Pattern grammar (one rule for the verifier): repository-relative, case-sensitive,
  full-path match; `*` matches within one path segment, `**` matches any depth; no
  basename or substring match. Reserved beats every group; a path in no group
  refers. Defaults live only in this file; the skill links it and restates no list.

- **D4 — Verifier `merge-risk-evidence.sh` with private `lib/merge-risk.py` (AC1,
  AC3, AC5, AC7).** [A] One deep Module: collection of every input through
  `gh`/`git`, then one pure evaluation function over the collected bundle. Deletion
  test: without it, config parsing, path matching, digesting and record checks
  would be redone by each caller and in prose, so it earns its Depth. Two real
  Adapters, no speculative Seam: the live `gh`/`git` collector, and a JSON bundle
  for tests (`python3 -I lib/merge-risk.py evaluate --bundle <file>`; the bundle
  carries `now`). Read-only: it never merges, labels, comments or votes.

  Interface: `merge-risk-evidence.sh [--phase class|final] <pr-number>` (default
  `final`) and `merge-risk-evidence.sh --queue`. Stdout: first line
  `merge-risk: <verdict> pr=<n> head=<H> base=<B> diff=<sha256> config=<C>`, then
  one `reason: <code> <detail>` line per reason, all reasons, stable codes. Exit
  codes: `0` eligible, `1` held, `3` referred, `4` unresolved, `2` usage. Any other
  exit, a crash, or missing `gh`/`python3` is read by callers as unresolved.
  Verdict precedence when several apply: referred, then unresolved, then held (a
  referral is never downgraded by missing evidence).

  `--phase class` (before the panel is convened; may run while CI is pending, then
  answers `unresolved` with reason `gates-pending`): config valid, `enabled` with
  acceptance; repository match; base is `main`; head not in `release_heads`; exactly
  one closing issue reference (`closingIssuesReferences`); B = current `main` tip
  and `merge-base(B, H) == B` (else `unresolved behind-base`); file list, rename old
  paths, additions and deletions from the B...H compare (binary or unmeasurable
  file: unresolved); caps; group and reserved matching; a `CHANGES.md` hunk that
  changes a `**Meaning version:**` line: referred; any review ever in state
  `CHANGES_REQUESTED`: referred; labels on PR, work-item issue and control issue;
  control issue open; `merge-preflight.sh <n>` run with
  `CLAUDE_WORKFLOW_MERGE_GUARD_OFF` removed from its environment, exit 0 and no
  `warning:` line on stderr; required check `check` completed `SUCCESS` on H (run ID
  recorded); diff digest = SHA-256 of the exact B..H unified diff bytes.

  `--phase final` adds: exactly one decision record (D5) for H on the work-item
  issue, never edited (`updated_at == created_at`); its H, B, diff and C equal the
  current values; five rows, roles distinct and complete; each source URL resolves,
  its body SHA-256 equals the row, it contains exactly one position line whose role
  matches, and (Product, Architect, QA, Reviewer) its first line is a `model-record`
  marker whose stage matches the role (existing reader in `lib/model-record.sh`);
  every row `yes`/`yes-if` with the same A and D digests; floor numbers: each voter
  score at least the highest author score, every entry with model, variant, score,
  date; Reviewer assertions present and `none` (D5); `now - T >= hold_seconds`
  (else `held hold-window`, with the earliest time); no `labels.hold` or
  `labels.off` label added on PR, issue or control issue at any time after T (from
  the timeline; else `unresolved void-after-announcement`, needing a new record and
  a new window); `executor_host` non-empty and equal to `hostname -s`.

  `--queue`: lists every queue entry on the control issue whose latest state is not
  terminal, for wake recovery (D7).

  What the verifier cannot decide, and so takes only as recorded assertions whose
  presence it checks: semantic disqualifiers (new security trade-off, spec-content
  decision, permission expansion, authority choice, weakened protection or oracle,
  outward-facing action, version or tag effect outside reserved paths, semantic
  change to the autonomy mechanism outside reserved paths), accepted-design lineage
  for guard paths and baseline lineage for ordinary paths, open medium/high
  findings, honest voter independence, and that the acceptance comment is the
  maintainer's. Byte-exact regeneration of generated outputs is carried by the
  required `check`, which runs `check-workflow-adapters.sh` [V `check` line 148].

- **D5 — Position line, decision record, manifest (AC2, AC4; reuses A54's shared
  record).** [A]
  - Position line, one per report:
    `merge-risk-position: role=<Product|Architect|QA|Reviewer|orchestrator> position=<yes-if|yes|no|abstain> ac=<sha256> design=<sha256|pending> head=<H|any>`,
    followed by a `conditions:` paragraph (scope, paths, what would void it).
    Product writes `design=pending head=any` (its yes-if delegates to the later
    accepted Planning digest for the same A); Architect and QA write `head=any`;
    the Reviewer writes `position=yes head=<H>` in its Review report; the
    orchestrator writes `position=yes head=<H>` in a marker-free issue comment
    (OR44) after its process check, sealed before it reads the Review conclusion
    (procedure). A `model-record` marker alone is never a position. A report
    without a position line cannot be reused and does not reduce the five: the role
    gets a new scoped record or the maintainer decides.
  - A and D: SHA-256 of the exact UTF-8 bytes of the accepted AC text (the issue
    body revision current at the acceptance comment's time) and of the A-entry text
    in `ARCHITECTURE.md` at a named commit; the manifest records both sources.
  - Decision record: one ordinary comment on the work-item issue in A54's shared
    format (literal `temporary, panel decision`, stable ID `MR-<pr>-<short H>-<n>`,
    question, positions, vote including dissent, outcome, rationale, reservation
    status, limit/risk flag) plus, in a fenced block opened by
    `<!-- merge-risk-manifest v1 -->`, one JSON object: `decision_id`,
    `repository`, `issue`, `pr`, `head`, `base`, `diff_sha256`, `config_sha256`,
    `config_commit`, `ac {source, sha256}`, `design {source, sha256}`, `class`,
    `reasons`, `authors [{model, variant, score, entry, date}]`, `rows [{role,
    source_url, source_sha256, position, model, variant, score, entry, date}]`,
    `gates {preflight, check_run_id}`, `reviewer_assertions {semantic_disqualifiers,
    lineage, open_medium_high}`, `hold_release` (null or link plus verbatim
    words), `outcome`, `earliest_merge`, `labels`, `executor_host`, `queue_key`,
    `revert: "pending"`. Its server `created_at` is the announcement time T. Every
    outcome (eligible, held, vetoed, unresolved, referred, failed, merged) gets a
    record; only `eligible` starts a window. The PR description links the record
    beside `Closes #<work-item>`.
  - Completion: a new comment linked to the record (never an edit, so the no-edit
    check stays valid) with merged H, time, squash SHA and the exact
    `git revert <squash-SHA>`. Reversal is a normal maintainer-confirmed revert PR.
  - Disclosure (AC4): merge-risk records are listed in their own 5-0 group,
    dissent and unresolved visible, no invented 3-0/2-1 (A54's grouping applied).

- **D6 — Hold (AC5; maintainer decisions D3, D6, D7).** [A] T is the decision
  record's server `created_at`; earliest merge is `T + hold_seconds` (at the default
  299 s waits, 300 s may proceed). A spoken hold (session or relay) becomes the
  `hold` label at once; the label is added by the maintainer or a voter (Q2; on the
  shared login the verifier cannot tell who, so any hold label vetoes). Once a hold
  or risk label appears after T the record is void (D4 final phase), so release
  always needs a new record and a full new window. Only the maintainer releases his
  hold: the new record's `hold_release` quotes his verbatim words for that PR with
  their link; the verifier checks the field is present, not who wrote it. No risk
  label existing anywhere is a valid state (dormant veto), never evidence of safety.

- **D7 — Executor, recheck of `main`, recovery, revocation (AC7).** [A] The
  executor is the orchestrator session on the machine named by `executor_host`, one
  PR at a time. Sequence per item, each step logged in the Pipeline log:
  1. `merge-risk-evidence.sh --phase final <n>`: exit 0, else wait (1) or refer.
  2. Queue comment on the control issue:
     `merge-risk-queue: id=<decision_id> pr=<n> head=<H> state=executing host=<host>`.
  3. `merge-preflight.sh <n>` fresh: exit 0 without warnings.
  4. The literal Bash command
     `gh pr merge <n> --repo TiesL/spec-driven-guardrails --squash --delete-branch --match-head-commit <H>`,
     never wrapped in a script, so the PreToolUse merge guard and
     `stop-after-completion` see it.
  5. `gh pr view <n> --json state,mergeCommit,headRefOid`: `MERGED` with
     `headRefOid == H` gives the completion comment and a `state=merged` queue line;
     anything else gives `state=failed`, a record and a referral.
  6. Before the next item: `git fetch origin`, then step 1 for it. Its manifest
     names the old B, so it is `unresolved` until update-branch, CI, a delta Review,
     a new orchestrator check, a new manifest and a new window.
  Recovery: a wake or resumed session runs `--queue` first; an `executing` entry is
  reconciled against the PR's actual state before anything else (merged: record
  completion; still open: refer, never retry blindly); an unknown outcome stops and
  refers. Queue lines are append-only, keyed `(repository, pr, H, decision_id)`; a
  key executes at most once. Comments and labels are not a lock; `executor_host`
  prevents an accidental second machine, not a deliberate one.
  Revocation: `merge-autonomy:off` on the control issue, `enabled: false`, a closed
  control issue or a config digest change turns every pending decision into a
  maintainer-approval item (old records do not revive: the C check or the void
  check fails them). The label on one PR or issue refers that item. Only the
  maintainer re-enables (config PR or label removal, then new records). An
  incorrect autonomous merge, an ignored hold or suspected forgery: add the global
  off label, record the incident on the control issue, refer.

- **D8 — Human path, releases, self-application, statistics (AC6, AC8).** [A]
  Outside C5, any disqualifier, dissent, missing evidence or revoked autonomy:
  today's rule with all lapse rules of step 4. An explicit maintainer approval of an
  in-class PR is a human-path merge, recorded as such. Relays and wakes count only
  his verbatim words about that exact PR and decision. Release-into-`main` and
  work-item-into-release merges are untouched. #646's own PR touches reserved paths
  and cannot merge under its delegation. Statistics per config revision (AC8) are a
  procedure: the orchestrator posts them on the control issue from the decision
  records (candidates, each reason, 5-0, holds, referrals, dissent, merges,
  failures, reverts, incidents, time to merge, token usage or `n/a`); no script in
  this work item. Widening only by a maintainer-approved config PR.

- **Mechanical versus procedure.**

  | Control | Enforced by |
  | --- | --- |
  | `check` green, branch up to date | GitHub branch protection, every merge [V] |
  | Review marker for H, behind-base, CI, role-play, stray Closes | `hooks/git-guardrails` on a literal Bash `gh pr merge` (Claude); `merge-preflight.sh` (Codex, instruction-driven) [V] |
  | Merge only at H | `--match-head-commit <H>` (server-side) |
  | Config validity, class, caps, reserved paths, labels, CHANGES_REQUESTED, meaning-version line, B/H/diff/C binding, five rows, hashes, markers, floor numbers, hold arithmetic, void-after-hold, executor host, queue state | The verifier, only when the orchestrator runs it and obeys its exit code |
  | That the verifier is run, that a spoken hold becomes a label, that briefs ask for position lines, semantic disqualifiers, lineage, findings, independence, who added or removed a label, who wrote the acceptance | Procedure and role judgment; not enforceable on a shared login |

  Nothing new intercepts `gh pr merge` for autonomy: an orchestrator that skips the
  verifier and merges a C5 PR without approval commits the same violation as
  today's unapproved merge, caught only by the records. A new hook was rejected: it
  would have to decide whether a human approval exists, which it cannot read either.

- **Files and ownership.** [A] Product: `PRD.md` F70-F74 after acceptance; issue
  text. QA (`TEST-SCENARIOS.md` only, IDs from S605 or the first free number at Test
